sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第031卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 31.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 31.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀二十三】起屠維大淵獻，盡強圉協洽，凡九年。

translations.literal: [Han Annals 23] From Tuyu Dayuanxian through Qiangyu Xiehe; nine years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Han Annals 23] From Tuyu Dayuanxian through Qiangyu Xiehe—nine years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，三月，壬戌，隕石東郡八。

translations.literal: In spring, the third month, on renxu, eight meteorites fell in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, on renxu, eight meteorites fell in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，穎川鐵官徙申屠聖等百八十人殺長吏，盜庫兵，自稱將軍，經歷九郡。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, one hundred eighty Yingchuan iron-office convict laborers led by Shen Tu Sheng killed their senior officials, stole arsenal weapons, styled themselves generals, and passed through nine commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, one hundred eighty Yingchuan iron-office convicts led by Shen Tu Sheng killed their senior officials, looted the arsenal, proclaimed themselves generals, and rampaged through nine commanderies.

sentences.zh: 遣丞相長史、御史中丞逐捕，以軍興從事，皆伏辜。

translations.literal: The Chancellor's chief clerk and the Vice Censor-in-Chief were sent to pursue and capture them; prosecuted under emergency military law, all paid the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor's chief clerk and the Vice Censor-in-Chief were sent in pursuit; prosecuted under emergency military law, all were executed.

sentences.zh: 秋，王鳳疾，天子數自臨問，親執其手涕泣曰：「將軍病，如有不可言，平阿侯譚次將軍矣！

translations.literal: In autumn, Wang Feng fell ill; the Son of Heaven repeatedly visited him in person, took his hand in tears, and said: "General, you are ill—if there is something you cannot speak, Marquis of Ping'a Tan is next in line after you!
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Wang Feng fell ill; the emperor visited him again and again, took his hand in tears, and said: "General, you are ill—if there is something you cannot bring yourself to say, Marquis of Ping'a Tan stands next in line after you!

sentences.zh: 」鳳頓首泣曰：「譚等雖與臣至親，行皆奢僭，無以率導百姓，不如御史大夫音謹敕，臣敢以死保之！

translations.literal: " Feng prostrated himself weeping and said: "Though Tan and the others are my closest kin, their conduct is all extravagant and transgressive—they cannot lead and guide the common people. The Censor-in-Chief Yin is cautious and restrained; I dare guarantee him with my life!
translations.idiomatic: " Feng prostrated himself, weeping: "Though Tan and the others are my closest kin, they are all extravagant and overreaching and cannot lead the people. Censor-in-Chief Yin is cautious and disciplined—I dare stake my life on him!

sentences.zh: 」及鳳且死，上疏謝上，復固薦音自代，言譚等五人必不可用；

translations.literal: " As Feng neared death, he submitted a memorial thanking the emperor and again firmly recommended Yin to replace him, saying Tan and the other five men absolutely could not be used;
translations.idiomatic: " As Feng neared death, he submitted a memorial of thanks and again pressed Yin as his successor, declaring that Tan and the other five were utterly unfit;

sentences.zh: 天子然之。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven approved.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，譚倨，不肯事鳳，而音敬鳳，卑恭如子，故鳳薦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tan had been arrogant and unwilling to serve Feng, whereas Yin respected Feng, humble and deferential as a son—hence Feng recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Tan had been proud and refused to defer to Feng, while Yin honored him with a son's humility—hence Feng recommended him.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁巳，鳳薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingsi, Feng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingsi, Feng died.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲子，以王音為大司馬、車騎將軍，而王譚位特進，領城門兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiazi, Wang Yin was made Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry, while Wang Tan held the rank of Extraordinary Advancement and commanded the city-gate troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiazi, Wang Yin was appointed Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry; Wang Tan was given Extraordinary Advancement and command of the city-gate troops.

sentences.zh: 安定太守谷永以譚失職，勸譚辭讓，不受城門職；

translations.literal: Anding Administrator Gu Yong, because Tan had lost his post, urged Tan to decline and yield and not accept the city-gate office;
translations.idiomatic: Anding Administrator Gu Yong, seeing Tan displaced, urged him to decline and refuse the city-gate command;

sentences.zh: 由是譚、音相與不平。

translations.literal: thereby Tan and Yin became mutually resentful.
translations.idiomatic: thereafter Tan and Yin were at odds.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，丁卯，光祿勳於永為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on dingmao, Household Grandee Yu Yong became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on dingmao, Household Grandee Yu Yong was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 永，定國之子也。

translations.literal: Yong was the son of Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was the son of Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, the empire was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，雨雪。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, rain and snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, rain and snow fell.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，壬申，東平思王宇薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on renshen, King Si of Dongping, Yu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on renshen, King Si of Dongping, Yu, died.

sentences.zh: 少府王駿為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Wang Jun was made Metropolitan of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasurer Wang Jun was appointed Metropolitan of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 駿，吉之子也。

translations.literal: Jun was the son of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was the son of Ji.

sentences.zh: 先是，京兆有趙廣漢、張敞、王尊、王章、王駿，皆有能名，故京師稱曰：「前有趙、張，後有三王。

translations.literal: Before this, Jingzhao had Zhao Guanghan, Zhang Chang, Wang Zun, Wang Zhang, and Wang Jun—all famed for ability—so the capital said: "Before there were Zhao and Zhang; after, there are three Wangs.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Jingzhao had Zhao Guanghan, Zhang Chang, Wang Zun, Wang Zhang, and Wang Jun—all famed for ability—so the capital said: "Before there were Zhao and Zhang; after, there are the three Wangs.

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬戌，於永卒。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on renxu, Yu Yong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on renxu, Yu Yong died.

sentences.zh: 烏孫小昆彌烏就屠死，子拊離代立；

translations.literal: The Wusun junior Kunmi Wujiutu died; his son Fuli succeeded him;
translations.idiomatic: The Wusun junior Kunmi Wujiutu died; his son Fuli succeeded;

sentences.zh: 為弟日貳所殺。

translations.literal: and was killed by his younger brother Rier.
translations.idiomatic: and was killed by his younger brother Rier.

sentences.zh: 漢遣使者立拊離子安日為小昆彌。

translations.literal: Han sent an envoy to establish Fuli's son Anri as junior Kunmi.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent an envoy to install Fuli's son Anri as junior Kunmi.

sentences.zh: 日貳亡阻康居；

translations.literal: Rier fled and held out in Kangju;
translations.idiomatic: Rier fled and held out in Kangju;

sentences.zh: 安日使貴人姑莫匿等三人詐亡從日貳，刺殺之。

translations.literal: Anri sent three honored men, Gu Mo'ni and others, who feigned flight to join Rier and stabbed him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Anri sent three nobles, including Gu Mo'ni, who pretended to defect to Rier and assassinated him.

sentences.zh: 於是西域諸國上書，願復得前都護段會宗；

translations.literal: Thereupon the states of the Western Regions submitted memorials asking again to have the former Protector Duan Huizong;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Western Regions submitted memorials asking that former Protector Duan Huizong be restored;

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: the emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 城郭諸國聞之，皆翕然親附。

translations.literal: The walled states, hearing it, all warmly drew near and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The walled states, hearing this, all drew close and rallied to Han.

sentences.zh: 谷永奏言：「聖王不以名譽加於實效；

translations.literal: Gu Yong memorialized: "Sage kings do not add reputation beyond actual achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong memorialized: "Sage kings do not heap reputation upon what has not been achieved;

sentences.zh: 御史大夫任重職大，少府宣達於從政，唯陛下留神考察！

translations.literal: the Censor-in-Chief bears weighty duties in a great office; Privy Treasurer Xuan is accomplished at participating in government—only Your Majesty, please examine with care!
translations.idiomatic: the Censor-in-Chief bears a weighty office; Privy Treasurer Xuan is adept in government—may Your Majesty examine them with care!

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，以薛宣為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi, Xue Xuan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guisi, Xue Xuan was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬午，上行幸初陵，赦作徒；

translations.literal: In the second month, on renwu, the emperor traveled in favor to the first imperial tomb and pardoned convict laborers;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renwu, the emperor visited the first imperial tomb and pardoned convict laborers;

sentences.zh: 以新豐戲鄉為昌陵縣，奉初陵。

translations.literal: Xinfeng's Xi township was made Changling county to serve the first tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Xinfeng's Xi township was made Changling county to supply the first tomb.

sentences.zh: 上始為微行，從期門郎或私奴十餘人，或乘小車，或皆騎，出入市裡郊野，遠至旁縣甘泉、長楊、五柞，鬥雞、走馬，常自稱富平侯家人。

translations.literal: The emperor began traveling incognito, with a dozen or so palace guard officers or private slaves, sometimes riding in a small cart, sometimes all on horseback, going in and out of markets, lanes, and suburbs, as far as neighboring counties Sweet Springs, Changyang, and Wuzuo—cockfighting and horse-racing—and often calling himself a member of the household of Marquis of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor began traveling in disguise, accompanied by a dozen palace guards or private slaves, sometimes in a small cart, sometimes all mounted, roaming markets, suburbs, and neighboring counties as far as Sweet Springs, Changyang, and Wuzuo—cockfighting and racing horses—and often passing himself off as kin of the Marquis of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 富平侯者，張安世四世孫放也。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Fuping was Fang, fourth-generation descendant of Zhang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Fuping was Fang, fourth-generation descendant of Zhang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 放父臨，尚敬武公主，生放，放為侍中、中郎將，娶許皇后女弟，當時寵幸無比，故假稱之。

translations.literal: Fang's father Lin had married Princess Jingwu and fathered Fang; Fang was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Gentleman, and married the Empress Xu's younger sister by a sister—then the most favored without compare—hence the false claim.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's father Lin had married Princess Jingwu and fathered him; Fang served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Gentleman and married the Empress Xu's sister-in-law—then the most favored man at court—hence the borrowed name.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚戌，張禹以老病罷，以列侯朝朔、望，位特進，見禮如丞相，賞賜前後數千萬。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengxu, Zhang Yu was dismissed for age and illness; as a ranked marquis he attended court on the first and fifteenth of the month, held Extraordinary Advancement, received rites like a Chancellor, and was rewarded before and after to the tune of tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengxu, Zhang Yu retired for age and illness; as a ranked marquis he attended court on the first and fifteenth, held Extraordinary Advancement, was treated like a Chancellor, and received rewards totaling tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰，薛宣為丞相，封高陽侯；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengchen, Xue Xuan became Chancellor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengchen, Xue Xuan was made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoyang;

sentences.zh: 京兆尹王駿為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Metropolitan of Jingzhao Wang Jun became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan of Jingzhao Wang Jun was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 王音既以從舅越親用事，小心親職。

translations.literal: Wang Yin, because as maternal uncle he held power beyond the proper degree of kinship, carefully attended to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, wielding power as a maternal uncle closer than custom allowed, carefully minded his office.

sentences.zh: 上以音自御史大夫入為將軍，不獲宰相之封，六月，乙巳，封音為安陽侯。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yin had entered the generalship from the Censor-in-Chiefship without receiving a chancellor's enfeoffment, in the sixth month, on yisi, enfeoffed Yin as Marquis of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yin had risen from Censor-in-Chief to general without receiving a chancellor's marquisate, in the sixth month, on yisi, the emperor enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，黃龍見真定。

translations.literal: In winter, a yellow dragon was seen in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, a yellow dragon was seen in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 是歲，匈奴復株累單于死，弟且糜胥立，為搜諧若鞮單于；

translations.literal: This year, the Xiongnu Chanyu Fuzhulei died; his younger brother Qiemixi succeeded as Chanyu Souxie Ruodi;
translations.idiomatic: This year, the Xiongnu Chanyu Fuzhulei died; his younger brother Qiemixi succeeded as Chanyu Souxie Ruodi;

sentences.zh: 遣子左祝都韓王呴留斯侯入侍，以且莫車為左賢王。

translations.literal: he sent his son, Left Zhudu Han King Xuliusihou, to attend at court, and made Chemoche Left Wise King.
translations.idiomatic: he sent his son, Left Zhudu Han King Xuliusihou, to attend at court and made Chemoche Left Wise King.

sentences.zh: 春，上行幸雲陽、甘泉。

translations.literal: In spring, the emperor traveled in favor to Yunyang and Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the emperor traveled to Yunyang and Sweet Springs.

sentences.zh: 三月，博士行大射禮。

translations.literal: In the third month, the erudites performed the great archery rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the erudites performed the great archery rite.

sentences.zh: 有飛雉集於庭，歷階登堂而雊；

translations.literal: A flying pheasant gathered in the courtyard, ascended the steps, entered the hall, and called;
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant flew into the courtyard, climbed the steps, entered the hall, and crowed;

sentences.zh: 後雉又集太常、宗正、丞相、御史大夫、車騎將軍之府，又集未央宮承明殿屋上。

translations.literal: later the pheasant again gathered at the offices of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, Director of the Imperial Clan, Chancellor, Censor-in-Chief, and General of Chariots and Cavalry, and again atop the roof of Chenming Hall in Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: later it appeared at the offices of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, Director of the Imperial Clan, Chancellor, Censor-in-Chief, and General of Chariots and Cavalry, and finally on the roof of Chenming Hall in Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍音、待詔寵等上言：「天地之氣，以類相應；

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin, Attendant-at-Court Chong, and others submitted: "The qi of Heaven and Earth respond to one another by kind;
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin, Attendant-at-Court Chong, and others submitted: "Heaven and earth answer to one another by kind;

sentences.zh: 譴告人君，甚微而著。

translations.literal: reproving and warning the human ruler—very slight, yet manifest.
translations.idiomatic: reproving and warning the ruler—subtle, yet unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 雉者聽察，先聞雷聲，故《月令》以紀氣。

translations.literal: The pheasant is hearing and observing; it first hears the sound of thunder—hence the Monthly Ordinances records qi by it.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant hears and watches; it senses thunder before it comes—hence the Monthly Ordinances uses it to mark the seasons.

sentences.zh: 《經》載高宗雊雉之異，以明轉禍為福之驗。

translations.literal: The Classic records the anomaly of Gaozong's crowing pheasant to show the proof of turning calamity into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic records the omen of Gaozong's crowing pheasant to show how calamity may turn to blessing.

sentences.zh: 今雉以博士行禮之日大眾聚會，飛集於庭，歷階登堂，萬眾睢睢，驚怪連日，逕歷三公之府，太常、宗正典宗廟骨肉之官，然後入宮，其宿留告曉人，具備深切；

translations.literal: Now, on the day the erudites performed the rite, with the great crowd assembled, the pheasant flew and gathered in the courtyard, ascended the steps and entered the hall—ten thousand people gazing, alarmed and astonished for days on end—it passed straight through the offices of the three dukes, the Grand Master of Ceremonies and Director of the Imperial Clan who oversee the ancestral temples and flesh-and-blood kin, and only then entered the palace; its lodging and lingering to inform and awaken people was complete and profound;
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the day the erudites performed the rite, before a vast assembly, the bird flew into the courtyard, climbed the steps, and entered the hall—ten thousand eyes upon it, wonder and alarm for days—then passed through the three highest offices, the Grand Master of Ceremonies and Director of the Imperial Clan who guard the ancestral temples and royal kin, and only then entered the palace; its stay and its message were thorough and grave;

sentences.zh: 雖人道相戒，何以過是！

translations.literal: though the human way offers mutual warnings, how could any surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: what human warning could surpass this!

sentences.zh: 」後帝使中常侍晁閎詔音曰：「聞捕得雉，毛羽頗摧折，類拘執者，得無人為之？

translations.literal: " Later the emperor sent Palace Attendant Chao Hong with an edict to Yin: "We hear the captured pheasant's feathers were quite broken and bent, like one that had been confined—could there not have been human agency?
translations.idiomatic: " Later the emperor sent Palace Attendant Chao Hong to Yin with an edict: "We hear the captured pheasant's feathers were broken and bent, as if it had been confined—was this not someone's doing?

sentences.zh: 」音復對曰：「陛下安得亡國之語！

translations.literal: " Yin replied again: "Your Majesty, how can you entertain words of a state's destruction!
translations.idiomatic: " Yin replied again: "Your Majesty, how can you speak as if the state were doomed!

sentences.zh: 不知誰主為佞諂之計，誣亂聖德如此者！

translations.literal: Who knows what master plotted this flatterer's scheme to slander and confuse sage virtue to such a degree!
translations.idiomatic: Who devised this slanderous flattery to corrupt Your Majesty's virtue so!

sentences.zh: 左右阿諛甚眾，不待臣音復諂而足。

translations.literal: Those at your left and right fawn and flatter in great numbers—without waiting for me Yin to flatter again, there are already enough.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers crowd your side; they need no help from me.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下，保位自守，莫有正言。

translations.literal: From the dukes and ministers down, all guard their posts and keep themselves—none offers upright speech.
translations.idiomatic: From the highest ministers down, all cling to their posts; none speaks plainly.

sentences.zh: 如令陛下覺寤，懼大禍且至身，深責臣下，繩以聖法，臣音當先誅，豈有以自解哉！

translations.literal: If now Your Majesty should awaken, fearing that great calamity is about to reach your person, and deeply blame your subordinates, binding them with sage law—I Yin ought to be executed first; how could there be any way to excuse myself!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty should awaken, fear great calamity drawing near, and bind your ministers with the full force of law—I should be executed first; how could I excuse myself!

sentences.zh: 今即位十五年，繼嗣不立，日日駕車而出，失行流聞；

translations.literal: Now you have reigned fifteen years, yet no heir is established; day after day you drive your carriage and go out, and misconduct spreads by rumor;
translations.idiomatic: You have reigned fifteen years without establishing an heir; day after day you drive abroad, and scandal spreads;

sentences.zh: 海內傳之，甚於京師。

translations.literal: within the seas it is transmitted, more than in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: throughout the realm it travels, louder than within the capital.

sentences.zh: 外有微行之害，內有疾病之憂，皇天數見災異，欲人變更，終已不改。

translations.literal: Externally there is the harm of incognito travel; internally there is worry over illness; August Heaven repeatedly shows disaster and anomaly, wishing people to change and reform—yet in the end you do not change.
translations.idiomatic: Without, disguise roams abroad; within, illness gnaws; Heaven shows omens again and again, urging change—yet you do not change.

sentences.zh: 天尚不能感動陛下，臣子何望！

translations.literal: If even Heaven cannot move Your Majesty, what can ministers hope for!
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven itself cannot move you, what hope have your ministers!

sentences.zh: 獨有極言待死，命在朝暮而已。

translations.literal: I have only extreme speech while awaiting death—my fate hangs on dawn and dusk.
translations.idiomatic: I have only blunt words and await death; my life hangs on the morrow.

sentences.zh: 如有不然，老母安得處所，尚何皇太后之有！

translations.literal: If it were otherwise, where could my old mother find a dwelling—how would there still be an Empress Dowager!
translations.idiomatic: If it were otherwise, where would my mother find shelter—what Empress Dowager would remain!

sentences.zh: 高祖天下當以誰屬乎！

translations.literal: To whom should the realm of the High Ancestor be entrusted!
translations.idiomatic: To whom should the High Ancestor's realm pass!

sentences.zh: 宜謀於賢智，克己復禮，以求天意，繼嗣可立，災變尚可銷也。

translations.literal: You ought to take counsel with the worthy and wise, restrain yourself and restore ritual, to seek Heaven's intent—the heir can be established, and disaster and anomaly may still be dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: Take counsel with the wise, restrain yourself and restore ritual, seek Heaven's will—then an heir may be named and the omens dispelled.

sentences.zh: 初，元帝儉約，渭陵不復徙民起邑；

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Yuan was frugal; at Weiling he did not again relocate people to build a city;
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Emperor Yuan was frugal; at Weiling he did not relocate people to build a city;

sentences.zh: 帝起初陵，數年後，樂霸陵曲亭南，更營之。

translations.literal: this emperor built the first tomb; several years later, delighted with the area south of Baling's Qu pavilion, he rebuilt it there.
translations.idiomatic: this emperor began the first tomb; years later, taken with the land south of Baling's Qu pavilion, he moved the site.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠解萬年使陳湯為奏，請為初陵徙民起邑，欲自以為功，求重賞。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Works Jie Wannian had Chen Tang memorialize, requesting that people be relocated to build a city for the first tomb—wishing to make it his own merit and seek a heavy reward.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of Works Jie Wannian had Chen Tang petition to relocate people and build a city for the first tomb, seeking merit and a rich reward.

sentences.zh: 湯因自請先徙，冀得美田宅。

translations.literal: Tang therefore requested to relocate first himself, hoping to obtain fine fields and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Tang asked to relocate first himself, hoping for fine lands and houses.

sentences.zh: 上從其言，果起昌陵邑。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words, and indeed built Changling city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and Changling city was built.

sentences.zh: 夏，徙郡國豪桀貲五百萬以上五千戶於昌陵。

translations.literal: In summer, five thousand households of powerful families from the commanderies and states with wealth of five million or more were relocated to Changling.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, five thousand wealthy households from across the empire—each worth five million or more—were moved to Changling.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸未，隕石於杜郵三。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guiwei, three meteorites fell at Duyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guiwei, three meteorites fell at Duyou.

sentences.zh: 六月，立中山憲王孫雲客為廣德王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the grandson of King Xian of Zhongshan, Yunke, was established as King of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yunke, grandson of King Xian of Zhongshan, was made King of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 是歲，城陽哀王雲薨；

translations.literal: This year, King Ai of Chengyang, Yun, died;
translations.idiomatic: This year, King Ai of Chengyang, Yun, died;

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: without sons; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: without heirs; the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，赦天下。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the empire was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 大旱。

translations.literal: A great drought.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought struck.

sentences.zh: 王氏五侯爭以奢侈相尚。

translations.literal: The five marquises of the Wang clan vied to regard one another in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The five Wang marquises vied in extravagance.

sentences.zh: 成都侯商嘗病，欲避暑，從上借明光宮。

translations.literal: Marquis of Chengdu Shang, once ill, wished to escape the heat and borrowed Bright Light Palace from the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Chengdu Shang, when ill, asked to borrow Bright Light Palace to escape the heat.

sentences.zh: 後又穿長安城，引內灃水，注第中大陂以行船，立羽蓋，張周帷，楫棹越歌。

translations.literal: Later he also bored through Chang'an's city wall, led Feng water inside, poured it into a great pond in his residence to sail boats, set feather canopies, spread perimeter curtains, and rowed to the songs of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he bored through Chang'an's wall, diverted Feng water into a great pond at his mansion for boating, raised feathered canopies and circling curtains, and rowed to Yue songs.

sentences.zh: 上幸商第，見穿城引水，意恨，內銜之，未言；

translations.literal: The emperor visited Shang's residence, saw the boring through the city to lead water, felt resentment, inwardly bore a grudge, but did not speak;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Shang's mansion, saw the breach and the waterworks, seethed inwardly, and said nothing;

sentences.zh: 後微行出，過曲陽侯第，又見園中土山、漸台，像白虎殿。

translations.literal: later, going out incognito, he passed the residence of Marquis of Quyang and again saw in the garden an earthen mound and a gradual terrace resembling White Tiger Hall.
translations.idiomatic: later, abroad in disguise, he passed Marquis of Quyang's mansion and saw an earthen hill and terraced pavilion in the garden mimicking White Tiger Hall.

sentences.zh: 於是上怒，以讓車騎將軍音。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was angry and reproached General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and rebuked General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin.

sentences.zh: 商、根兄弟欲自黥、劓以謝太后。

translations.literal: Shang and Gen, brothers, wished to tattoo and slash their own noses to apologize to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers Shang and Gen offered to tattoo and mutilate themselves before the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大怒，乃使尚書責問司隸校尉、京兆尹，知成都侯商等奢僭不軌，藏匿奸猾，皆阿縱，不舉奏正法；

translations.literal: The emperor heard it and was greatly angry; he then sent the Palace Clerk to reprove the Metropolitan Commandant and Metropolitan of Jingzhao—knowing that Marquis of Chengdu Shang and others were extravagant, transgressive, and improper, concealing crafty and wicked men, all fawning and indulging them, not memorializing to execute the proper law;
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor was furious and sent the Palace Clerk to rebuke the Metropolitan Commandant and Metropolitan of Jingzhao—for knowing that Marquis of Chengdu Shang and others lived in extravagance beyond law, sheltered villains, and fawned on them without prosecuting;

sentences.zh: 二人頓首省戶下。

translations.literal: the two men prostrated themselves with their heads below the office gate.
translations.idiomatic: both men prostrated themselves at the office gate.

sentences.zh: 又賜車騎將軍音策書曰：「外家何甘樂禍敗！

translations.literal: He again granted General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin an edict book saying: "Why would the consort kin gladly welcome calamity and ruin!
translations.idiomatic: He also sent General Yin an edict: "Why do the consort kin court disaster!

sentences.zh: 而欲自黥、劓，相戮辱於太后前，傷慈母之心，以危亂國家！

translations.literal: Yet you wish to tattoo and slash yourselves, mutually humiliating one another before the Empress Dowager, wounding your loving mother's heart and thereby endangering and disrupting the state!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would mutilate yourselves and shame one another before the Empress Dowager, wounding your mother's heart and endangering the realm!

sentences.zh: 外家宗族強，上一身浸弱日久，今將一施之，君其召諸侯，令待府捨！

translations.literal: The consort kin's clan is strong while the ruler above grows ever weaker day by day—now I am about to apply it once; you ought to summon the marquises and order them to wait at their mansions!
translations.idiomatic: Your clan grows strong while I grow weak—now I shall act; summon the marquises and keep them at their mansions!

sentences.zh: 」是日，詔尚書奏文帝時誅將軍薄昭故事。

translations.literal: " That day, an edict ordered the Palace Clerk to memorialize the precedent of Emperor Wen's execution of General Bo Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: " That day he ordered the Palace Clerk to cite Emperor Wen's execution of General Bo Zhao.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍音藉稿請罪，商、立、根皆負斧質謝，良久乃已。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin, on a straw mat, requested punishment; Shang, Li, and Gen all bore the axe-block and apologized—a long while before it ended.
translations.idiomatic: General Yin lay on straw and begged punishment; Shang, Li, and Gen came bearing the axe-block to plead—all for a long while before the storm passed.

sentences.zh: 上特欲恐之，實無意誅也。

translations.literal: The emperor specially wished to frighten them; he truly had no intent to execute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant only to terrify them; he had no real intent to kill.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，乙卯，孝景廟北闕災。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on yimao, the northern gate-tower of Emperor Xiaojing's temple burned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on yimao, the northern gate-tower of Emperor Jing's temple burned.

sentences.zh: 初，許皇后與班婕妤皆有寵於上。

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Fair Attendant all had favor with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Fair Attendant both enjoyed the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 上嘗游後庭，欲與婕妤同輦載，婕妤辭曰：「觀古圖畫，賢聖之君皆有名臣在側，三代末主乃有嬖妾。

translations.literal: The emperor once toured the rear garden and wished to ride in the same carriage with the Fair Attendant; she declined, saying: "Looking at ancient pictures, sage and worthy rulers all had famous ministers at their side; only the last rulers of the Three Dynasties had favorite concubines.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once toured the rear garden and wished to ride in the same carriage with the Fair Attendant; she declined, saying, "Looking at ancient pictures, sage and worthy rulers all had famous ministers at their side; only the last rulers of the Three Dynasties had favorite concubines.

sentences.zh: 今欲同輦，得無近似之乎！

translations.literal: Now if we wish to ride together, might this not be close to that!
translations.idiomatic: Now if we wish to ride together, might this not be close to that!

sentences.zh: 」上善其言而止。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved her words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved her words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，喜曰：「古有樊姬，今有班婕妤！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager heard it and said with joy: "Ancient times had Lady Fan; today there is Lady Ban the Fair Attendant!
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager heard it and said with joy, "Ancient times had Lady Fan; today there is Lady Ban the Fair Attendant!

sentences.zh: 」班婕妤進侍者李平得幸，亦為婕妤，賜姓曰衛。

translations.literal: " Lady Ban the Fair Attendant advanced her attendant Li Ping, who obtained favor, was also made Fair Attendant, and was granted the surname Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Ban the Fair Attendant advanced her attendant Li Ping, who obtained favor, was also made Fair Attendant, and was granted the surname Wei.

sentences.zh: 其後，上微行過陽阿主家，悅歌舞者趙飛燕，召入宮，大幸；

translations.literal: Afterward, the emperor went out incognito and passed the house of Princess Yang'a; he delighted in the song-and-dance performer Zhao Feiyan, summoned her into the palace, and greatly favored her;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, the emperor went out incognito and passed the house of Princess Yang'a; he delighted in the song-and-dance performer Zhao Feiyan, summoned her into the palace, and greatly favored her;

sentences.zh: 有女弟，復召入，姿性尤醲粹，左右見之，皆嘖嘖嗟賞。

translations.literal: she had a younger sister, who was again summoned in; her bearing and nature were especially rich and pure, and those beside her, seeing her, all clicked their tongues in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: she had a younger sister, who was again summoned in; her bearing and nature were especially rich and pure, and those beside her, seeing her, all clicked their tongues in admiration.

sentences.zh: 有宣帝時披香博士淖方成在帝后，唾曰：「此禍水也，滅火必矣！

translations.literal: There was the Poxiang erudite Zhuo Fangcheng from Emperor Xuan's time behind the emperor; he spat and said: "This is calamity-water; it will surely extinguish the fire!
translations.idiomatic: There was the Poxiang erudite Zhuo Fangcheng from Emperor Xuan's time behind the emperor; he spat and said, "This is calamity-water; it will surely extinguish the fire!

sentences.zh: 」姊、弟俱為婕妤，貴傾後宮。

translations.literal: " The elder and younger sisters were both made Fair Attendants, and their nobility overwhelmed the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The elder and younger sisters were both made Fair Attendants, and their nobility overwhelmed the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 許皇后、班婕妤皆失寵。

translations.literal: Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Fair Attendant all lost favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Fair Attendant both lost favor.

sentences.zh: 於是趙飛燕譖告許皇后、班婕妤挾媚道，祝詛後宮，詈及主上。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Feiyan slandered, reporting that Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Fair Attendant employed seductive arts, prayed and cursed against the inner palace, and reviled even the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhao Feiyan slandered, reporting that Empress Xu and Lady Ban the Fair Attendant employed seductive arts, prayed and cursed against the inner palace, and reviled even the ruler.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，甲寅，許後廢處昭台宮，後姊謁等皆誅死，親屬歸故郡。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiayin, Empress Xu was deposed and lodged at Zhaotai Palace; the empress's elder sister Ye and others were all executed, and relatives returned to their former commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiayin, Empress Xu was deposed and lodged at Zhaotai Palace; the empress's elder sister Ye and others were all executed, and relatives returned to their former commanderies.

sentences.zh: 考問班婕妤，婕妤對曰：「妾聞『死生有命，富貴在天。

translations.literal: Lady Ban the Fair Attendant was examined and questioned; she replied: "Your concubine has heard, 'Life and death have fate; wealth and honor are in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ban the Fair Attendant was examined and questioned; she replied, "Your concubine has heard, 'Life and death have fate; wealth and honor are in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 』修正尚未蒙福，為邪欲以何望！

translations.literal: ' Upright correction has not yet received blessing—doing evil, what could one hope for!
translations.idiomatic: ' Upright correction has not yet received blessing—doing evil, what could one hope for!

sentences.zh: 使鬼神有知，不受不臣之訴；

translations.literal: If ghosts and spirits have knowledge, they will not accept the appeal of the disloyal;
translations.idiomatic: If ghosts and spirits have knowledge, they will not accept the appeal of the disloyal;

sentences.zh: 如其無知，訴之何益！

translations.literal: if they have no knowledge, what use is appealing!
translations.idiomatic: if they have no knowledge, what use is appealing!

sentences.zh: 故不為也。

translations.literal: therefore I do not do it.
translations.idiomatic: therefore I do not do it.

sentences.zh: 」上善其對，赦之，賜黃金百斤。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved her reply, pardoned her, and bestowed a hundred jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved her reply, pardoned her, and bestowed a hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 趙氏姊、弟驕妒，婕妤恐久見危，乃求共養太后於長信宮。

translations.literal: The Zhao sisters were arrogant and jealous; the Fair Attendant feared that if seen long she would be endangered, and therefore requested to join in supporting the Empress Dowager at Changle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao sisters were arrogant and jealous; the Fair Attendant feared that if seen long she would be endangered, and therefore requested to join in supporting the Empress Dowager at Changle Palace.

sentences.zh: 上許焉。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 廣漢男子鄭躬等六十餘人攻官寺，篡囚徒，盜庫兵；

translations.literal: More than sixty men of Guanghan, including Zheng Gong, attacked government offices, seized prisoners, and stole arsenal weapons;
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty men of Guanghan, including Zheng Gong, attacked government offices, seized prisoners, and stole arsenal weapons;

sentences.zh: 自稱山君。

translations.literal: they styled themselves Lord of the Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: they styled themselves Lord of the Mountains.

sentences.zh: 秋，勃海、清河、信都河水湓溢，灌縣、邑三十一，敗官亭、民捨四萬餘所。

translations.literal: In autumn, the rivers of Bohai, Qinghe, and Xindu brimmed and overflowed, inundating thirty-one counties and districts and destroying more than forty thousand government lodges and commoners' dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the rivers of Bohai, Qinghe, and Xindu brimmed and overflowed, inundating thirty-one counties and districts and destroying more than forty thousand government lodges and commoners' dwellings.

sentences.zh: 平陵李尋等奏言：「議者常欲求索九河故跡而穿之。

translations.literal: Li Xun of Pingling and others memorialized, saying: "Deliberators have often wished to seek and trace the old courses of the Nine Rivers and cut through them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun of Pingling and others memorialized, saying, "Deliberators have often wished to seek and trace the old courses of the Nine Rivers and cut through them.

sentences.zh: 今因其自決，可且勿塞，以觀水勢；

translations.literal: Now, taking advantage of its bursting forth on its own, we may for the time not block it, to observe the water's force;
translations.idiomatic: Now, taking advantage of its bursting forth on its own, we may for the time not block it, to observe the water's force;

sentences.zh: 河欲居之，當稍自成川，跳出沙土。

translations.literal: if the river wishes to dwell there, it should gradually itself become a channel and leap out sand and soil.
translations.idiomatic: if the river wishes to dwell there, it should gradually itself become a channel and leap out sand and soil.

sentences.zh: 然後順天心而圖之，必有成功，而用財力寡。

translations.literal: Only afterward, following Heaven's heart and planning it, there will certainly be success, and the use of wealth and strength will be little.
translations.idiomatic: Only afterward, following Heaven's heart and planning it, there will certainly be success, and the use of wealth and strength will be little.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂止不塞。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they stopped and did not block.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they stopped and did not block.

sentences.zh: 朝臣數言百姓可哀，上遣使者處業振贍之。

translations.literal: Court ministers repeatedly said the common people were pitiable; the emperor sent envoys to settle affairs and relieve and sustain them.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers repeatedly said the common people were pitiable; the emperor sent envoys to settle affairs and relieve and sustain them.

sentences.zh: 廣漢鄭躬等黨與浸廣，犯歷四縣，眾且萬人；

translations.literal: The partisans of Zheng Gong of Guanghan gradually spread wider, offending and passing through four counties, their multitude nearly ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: The partisans of Zheng Gong of Guanghan gradually spread wider, offending and passing through four counties, their multitude nearly ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 州郡不能制。

translations.literal: the provinces and commanderies could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: the provinces and commanderies could not control them.

sentences.zh: 冬，以河東都尉趙護為廣漢太守，發郡中及蜀郡合三萬人擊之，或相捕斬除罪；

translations.literal: In winter, Commandant of Hedong Zhao Hu was made Administrator of Guanghan; he mobilized from within the commandery and from Shu Commandery together thirty thousand men to strike them, some capturing one another and beheading to expiate guilt;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Commandant of Hedong Zhao Hu was made Administrator of Guanghan; he mobilized from within the commandery and from Shu Commandery together thirty thousand men to strike them, some capturing one another and beheading to expiate guilt;

sentences.zh: 旬月平。

translations.literal: within a ten-day month it was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: within a month it was pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷護為執金吾，賜黃金百斤。

translations.literal: Hu was transferred to be Bearer of the Mace and was bestowed a hundred jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was transferred to be Bearer of the Mace and was bestowed a hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 是歲，平阿安侯王譚薨。

translations.literal: This year, Marquis of Ping'a and An Wang Tan died.
translations.idiomatic: This year, Marquis of Ping'a and An Wang Tan died.

sentences.zh: 上悔廢譚使不輔政而薨也，乃復成都侯商以特進領城門兵，置幕府，得舉吏如將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor regretted that Tan had been dismissed from assisting in government and then died; he therefore restored Marquis of Chengdu Shang as Special Advancement to lead the gate-tower troops, established a staff headquarters, and allowed him to recommend clerks like a general.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted that Tan had been dismissed from assisting in government and then died; he therefore restored Marquis of Chengdu Shang as Special Advancement to lead the gate-tower troops, established a staff headquarters, and allowed him to recommend clerks like a general.

sentences.zh: 魏郡杜鄴時為郎，素善車騎將軍音，見音前與平阿侯有隙，即說音曰：「夫戚而不見殊，孰能無怨！

translations.literal: Du Ye of Wei Commandery was then a Gentleman, and was always on good terms with General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin; seeing that Yin earlier had a rift with the Marquis of Ping'a, he immediately advised Yin, saying: "When kin are not shown distinction, who can be without resentment!
translations.idiomatic: Du Ye of Wei Commandery was then a Gentleman, and was always on good terms with General of Chariots and Cavalry Yin; seeing that Yin earlier had a rift with the Marquis of Ping'a, he immediately advised Yin, saying, "When kin are not shown distinction, who can be without resentment!

sentences.zh: 昔秦伯有千乘之國而不能容其母弟，《春秋》譏焉。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Mu of Qin had a state of a thousand chariots yet could not accommodate his younger brother by the same mother—the Spring and Autumn Annals reproved this.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Mu of Qin had a state of a thousand chariots yet could not accommodate his younger brother by the same mother—the Spring and Autumn Annals reproved this.

sentences.zh: 周、召則不然，忠以相輔，義以相匡，同己之親，等己之尊，不以聖德獨兼國寵，又不為長專受榮任，分職於陝，並為弼疑，故內無感恨之隙，外無侵侮之羞，俱享天祐，兩荷高名者，蓋以此也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao were not so—they were loyal in assisting one another and righteous in correcting one another, made kin like themselves and honor like themselves, did not because of sage virtue alone monopolize the state's favor, nor because of seniority alone specially receive glory and office; they divided duties at Shan and together were assistants and counselors—therefore within there was no gap of resentful feeling, without no shame of invasion and insult; both enjoyed Heaven's blessing and bore high names—this was roughly the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao were not so—they were loyal in assisting one another and righteous in correcting one another, made kin like themselves and honor like themselves, did not because of sage virtue alone monopolize the state's favor, nor because of seniority alone specially receive glory and office; they divided duties at Shan and together were assistants and counselors—therefore within there was no gap of resentful feeling, without no shame of invasion and insult; both enjoyed Heaven's blessing and bore high names—this was roughly the reason.

sentences.zh: 竊見成都侯以特進領城門兵，復有詔得舉吏如五府，此明詔所欲寵也。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that the Marquis of Chengdu, as Special Advancement, leads the gate-tower troops, and again has an edict allowing him to recommend clerks like the Five Offices—this shows clearly that the edict wishes to favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed that the Marquis of Chengdu, as Special Advancement, leads the gate-tower troops, and again has an edict allowing him to recommend clerks like the Five Offices—this shows clearly that the edict wishes to favor him.

sentences.zh: 將軍宜承順聖意，加異往時，每事凡議，必與及之。

translations.literal: The general ought to comply with and follow the sage intent, adding distinction beyond former times; in every matter, whenever there is deliberation, you must involve and reach him.
translations.idiomatic: The general ought to comply with and follow the sage intent, adding distinction beyond former times; in every matter, whenever there is deliberation, you must involve and reach him.

sentences.zh: 發於至誠，則孰不說諭！

translations.literal: Issuing from utmost sincerity, then who would not be pleased and instructed!
translations.idiomatic: Issuing from utmost sincerity, then who would not be pleased and instructed!

sentences.zh: 」音甚嘉其言，由是與成都侯商親密。

translations.literal: " Yin greatly approved his words; from this he became intimate with the Marquis of Chengdu Shang.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin greatly approved his words; from this he became intimate with the Marquis of Chengdu Shang.

sentences.zh: 二人皆重鄴。

translations.literal: Both men highly valued Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Both men highly valued Ye.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑，太官凌室火。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guichou, the ice storehouse of the Grand Provisioner caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guichou, the ice storehouse of the Grand Provisioner caught fire.

sentences.zh: 戊午，戾後園南闕火。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the southern gate-tower of the rear garden of the Deposed Empress caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the southern gate-tower of the rear garden of the Deposed Empress caught fire.

sentences.zh: 上欲立趙婕妤為皇后，皇太后嫌其所出微甚，難之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to establish Fair Attendant Zhao as empress; the Empress Dowager disliked that her origin was very slight and made it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to establish Fair Attendant Zhao as empress; the Empress Dowager disliked that her origin was very slight and made it difficult.

sentences.zh: 太后姊子淳于長為侍中，數往來通語東宮；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's sister's son Chunyu Chang was Attendant Within; he repeatedly went back and forth conveying words to the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's sister's son Chunyu Chang was Attendant Within; he repeatedly went back and forth conveying words to the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 歲餘，乃得太后指，許之。

translations.literal: after more than a year he finally obtained the Empress Dowager's intent and she assented.
translations.idiomatic: after more than a year he finally obtained the Empress Dowager's intent and she assented.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙亥，上先封婕妤父臨為成陽侯。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, the emperor first enfeoffed the Fair Attendant's father Lin as Marquis of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yihai, the emperor first enfeoffed the Fair Attendant's father Lin as Marquis of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 諫大夫河間劉輔上書，言：「昔武王、周公，承順天地以饗魚、鳥之瑞，然猶君臣示氐懼，動色相戒。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Liu Fu of Hejian submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, complying with Heaven and Earth, received the auspices of fish and birds—yet still ruler and ministers showed low fear, their expressions moving as they warned one another.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Liu Fu of Hejian submitted a memorial, saying, "Formerly King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, complying with Heaven and Earth, received the auspices of fish and birds—yet still ruler and ministers showed low fear, their expressions moving as they warned one another.

sentences.zh: 況於季世，不蒙繼嗣之福，屢受威怒之異者虖！

translations.literal: How much more in a declining age, not receiving the blessing of a successor, repeatedly receiving awesome-angry portents!
translations.idiomatic: How much more in a declining age, not receiving the blessing of a successor, repeatedly receiving awesome-angry portents!

sentences.zh: 雖夙夜自責，改過易行，畏天命，念祖業，妙選有德之世，考卜窈窕之女，以承宗廟，順神祇心，塞天下望，子孫之祥猶恐晚暮！

translations.literal: Though from dawn to night one blames oneself, changes faults and alters conduct, fears Heaven's mandate, and thinks on the ancestral enterprise—finely to select a worthy generation, examine and divine a modest and fair woman to continue the ancestral temple, follow the hearts of the spirits, and stop up the empire's hopes—even so, the auspice of sons and grandsons one still fears is late and twilight!
translations.idiomatic: Though from dawn to night one blames oneself, changes faults and alters conduct, fears Heaven's mandate, and thinks on the ancestral enterprise—finely to select a worthy generation, examine and divine a modest and fair woman to continue the ancestral temple, follow the hearts of the spirits, and stop up the empire's hopes—even so, the auspice of sons and grandsons one still fears is late and twilight!

sentences.zh: 今乃觸情縱欲，傾於卑賤之女，欲以母天下，不畏於天，不愧於人，惑莫大焉！

translations.literal: Now you touch feeling and indulge desire, leaning toward a slight and base woman, wishing to make her mother of the empire—not fearing Heaven, not ashamed before men—confusion could not be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Now you touch feeling and indulge desire, leaning toward a slight and base woman, wishing to make her mother of the empire—not fearing Heaven, not ashamed before men—confusion could not be greater!

sentences.zh: 裡語曰：『腐木不可以為柱；

translations.literal: A village saying goes: 'Rotten wood cannot serve as a pillar;
translations.idiomatic: A village saying goes, 'Rotten wood cannot serve as a pillar;

sentences.zh: 人婢不可以為主。

translations.literal: a person's bondmaid cannot serve as mistress.
translations.idiomatic: a person's bondmaid cannot serve as mistress.

sentences.zh: 』天人之所不予，必有禍而無福，市道皆共知之，朝廷莫肯壹言。

translations.literal: ' What Heaven and man do not grant must have calamity and not blessing; market and road all know it together, yet at court none will speak with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: ' What Heaven and man do not grant must have calamity and not blessing; market and road all know it together, yet at court none will speak with one voice.

sentences.zh: 臣竊傷心，不敢不盡死！

translations.literal: Your servant secretly is wounded at heart and dares not fail to exhaust death!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant secretly is wounded at heart and dares not fail to speak to the death!

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上使侍御史收縛輔，繫掖庭秘獄，群臣莫知其故。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor had the Attendant Censor arrest and bind Fu and imprison him in the secret prison of the Palace Domestic Service; the ministers all did not know the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor had the Attendant Censor arrest and bind Fu and imprison him in the secret prison of the Palace Domestic Service; the ministers all did not know the reason.

sentences.zh: 於是左將軍辛慶忌、右將軍廉褒、光祿勳琅邪師丹、太中大夫谷永俱上書曰：「竊見劉輔前以縣令求見，擢為諫大夫，此其言必有卓詭切至當聖心者，故得拔至於此；

translations.literal: Thereupon Left General Xin Qingji, Right General Lian Bao, Director of the Secretariat Shi Dan of Langye, and Grand Palace Counselor Gu Yong all submitted memorials, saying: "Your servant has observed that Liu Fu earlier, as a magistrate, sought audience and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee—his words must have had something outstanding, strange, and cutting that reached the sage heart, and therefore he was pulled up to this;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Left General Xin Qingji, Right General Lian Bao, Director of the Secretariat Shi Dan of Langye, and Grand Palace Counselor Gu Yong all submitted memorials, saying, "Your servant has observed that Liu Fu earlier, as a magistrate, sought audience and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee—his words must have had something outstanding, strange, and cutting that reached the sage heart, and therefore he was pulled up to this;

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，收下秘獄。

translations.literal: within a ten-day month he was taken down into the secret prison.
translations.idiomatic: within a month he was taken down into the secret prison.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚以為輔幸得托公族之親，在諫臣之列，新從下土來，未知朝廷體，獨觸忌諱，不足深過。

translations.literal: Your servants foolishly consider that Fu, fortunately obtaining to rely on kin of the ducal house, is in the ranks of remonstrating ministers, newly come from lower lands, and does not yet know the court's forms—alone touching taboo, not enough for a deep fault.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants foolishly consider that Fu, fortunately obtaining to rely on kin of the ducal house, is in the ranks of remonstrating ministers, newly come from lower lands, and does not yet know the court's forms—alone touching taboo, not enough for a deep fault.

sentences.zh: 小罪宜隱忍而已，如有大惡，宜暴治理官，與眾共之。

translations.literal: A small crime ought to be borne with in concealment only; if there is a great evil, it is fitting to expose and govern it through officials, sharing it with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: A small crime ought to be borne with in concealment only; if there is a great evil, it is fitting to expose and govern it through officials, sharing it with the multitude.

sentences.zh: 今天心未豫，災異屢降，水旱迭臻，方當隆寬廣問，褒直盡下之時也，而行慘急之誅於諫爭之臣，震驚群下，失忠直心。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's heart is not at ease, portents and anomalies repeatedly descend, flood and drought come in turn—it is just the time to exalt leniency, broaden inquiry, praise the upright, and bring all below—yet you carry out cruel and urgent punishment on a remonstrating minister, startling the multitude below and losing the heart of loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven's heart is not at ease, portents and anomalies repeatedly descend, flood and drought come in turn—it is just the time to exalt leniency, broaden inquiry, praise the upright, and bring all below—yet you carry out cruel and urgent punishment on a remonstrating minister, startling the multitude below and losing the heart of loyalty and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 假令輔不坐直言，所坐不著，天下不可戶曉。

translations.literal: Supposing Fu is not punished for blunt speech, yet the crime for which he sits is not clear—the empire cannot be made to know door by door.
translations.idiomatic: Supposing Fu is not punished for blunt speech, yet the crime for which he is punished is not clear—the empire cannot be made to know door by door.

sentences.zh: 同姓近臣，本以言顯，其於治親養忠之義，誠不宜幽囚於掖庭獄。

translations.literal: A kinsman of the same surname and a near minister, by origin made manifest through words—for the meaning of governing kin and nurturing loyalty, it truly is not fitting to be darkly imprisoned in the Palace Domestic Service prison.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of the same surname and a near minister, by origin made manifest through words—for the meaning of governing kin and nurturing loyalty, it truly is not fitting to be darkly imprisoned in the Palace Domestic Service prison.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下，見陛下進用輔亟而折傷之暴，人有懼心，精銳銷耎，莫敢盡節正言，非所以昭有虞之聽，廣德美之風！

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes down, seeing Your Majesty advance and employ Fu quickly yet break and wound him violently, men have a heart of fear; keen edge is worn away soft—none dare exhaust loyalty in upright speech; this is not the means to make manifest the listening of Youyu, or broaden the wind of virtue and beauty!
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dukes down, seeing Your Majesty advance and employ Fu quickly yet break and wound him violently, men have a heart of fear; keen edge is worn away soft—none dare exhaust loyalty in upright speech; this is not the means to make manifest the listening of Youyu, or broaden the wind of virtue and beauty!

sentences.zh: 臣等竊深傷之，惟陛下留神省察！

translations.literal: Your servants secretly are deeply wounded—only may Your Majesty keep your spirit and examine and reflect!
translations.idiomatic: Your servants secretly are deeply wounded—only may Your Majesty keep your spirit and examine and reflect!

sentences.zh: 」上乃徙繫輔共工獄，減死罪一等，論為鬼薪。

translations.literal: " The emperor then transferred Fu's imprisonment to the Works prison, reduced the death crime by one grade, and sentenced him to ghost firewood.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then transferred Fu's imprisonment to the Works prison, reduced the death crime by one grade, and sentenced him to ghost firewood.

sentences.zh: 初，太后兄弟八人，獨弟曼早死，不侯；

translations.literal: Earlier, the Empress Dowager's brothers were eight; only the younger brother Man died early and was not enfeoffed;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Empress Dowager's brothers were eight; only the younger brother Man died early and was not enfeoffed;

sentences.zh: 太后憐之。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager pitied him.

sentences.zh: 曼寡婦渠供養東宮，子莽幼孤，不及等比，其群兄弟皆將軍、五侯子，乘時侈靡，以輿馬聲色佚游相高。

translations.literal: Man's widow Qu supported the Eastern Palace; the son Mang was young and orphaned, not reaching equal comparison—the band of brothers were all sons of generals and the Five Marquises, riding the times in extravagant excess, competing high in carriages, horses, sound, color, and idle roaming.
translations.idiomatic: Man's widow Qu supported the Eastern Palace; the son Mang was young and orphaned, not reaching equal comparison—the band of brothers were all sons of generals and the Five Marquises, riding the times in extravagant excess, competing high in carriages, horses, sound, color, and idle roaming.

sentences.zh: 莽因折節為恭儉，勤身博學，被服如儒生；

translations.literal: Mang therefore bent his conduct to be respectful and frugal, toiled in body and broadly studied, his dress like a Confucian scholar;
translations.idiomatic: Mang therefore bent his conduct to be respectful and frugal, toiled in body and broadly studied, his dress like a Confucian scholar;

sentences.zh: 事母及寡嫂，養孤兄子，行甚敕備；

translations.literal: served his mother and widowed sister-in-law, reared his orphaned elder brother's son—his conduct very careful and complete;
translations.idiomatic: served his mother and widowed sister-in-law, reared his orphaned elder brother's son—his conduct very careful and complete;

sentences.zh: 又外交英俊，內事諸父，曲有禮意。

translations.literal: outwardly he befriended outstanding men; inwardly he served his various uncles, bending with ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly he befriended outstanding men; inwardly he served his various uncles, bending with ritual intent.

sentences.zh: 大將軍鳳病，莽侍疾，親嘗藥，亂首垢面，不解衣帶連月。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Feng fell ill; Mang attended the illness, personally tasted medicine, hair disordered and face filthy, not undoing belt or clothes for consecutive months.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Feng fell ill; Mang attended the illness, personally tasted medicine, hair disordered and face filthy, not undoing belt or clothes for consecutive months.

sentences.zh: 鳳且死，以托太后及帝，拜為黃門郎，遷射聲校尉。

translations.literal: When Feng was about to die, he entrusted him to the Empress Dowager and the emperor; Mang was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and transferred to Commandant of the Archers.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng was about to die, he entrusted him to the Empress Dowager and the emperor; Mang was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and transferred to Commandant of the Archers.

sentences.zh: 久之，叔父成都侯商上書，願分戶邑以封莽。

translations.literal: After a long time, his uncle the Marquis of Chengdu Shang submitted a memorial wishing to divide household fiefs to enfeoff Mang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, his uncle the Marquis of Chengdu Shang submitted a memorial wishing to divide household fiefs to enfeoff Mang.

sentences.zh: 長樂少府戴崇、侍中金涉、中郎陳湯等皆當世名士，咸為莽言，上由是賢莽，太后又數以為言。

translations.literal: Director of Changle Dai Chong, Attendant Within Jin She, Palace Gentleman Chen Tang, and others were all famous scholars of the age and all spoke for Mang; the emperor thereby esteemed Mang, and the Empress Dowager also repeatedly spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Changle Dai Chong, Attendant Within Jin She, Palace Gentleman Chen Tang, and others were all famous scholars of the age and all spoke for Mang; the emperor thereby esteemed Mang, and the Empress Dowager also repeatedly spoke on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙未，封莽為新都侯，遷騎都尉、光祿大夫、侍中。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yiwei, Mang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu, transferred to Commandant of Cavalry, Palace Counselor, and Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yiwei, Mang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu, transferred to Commandant of Cavalry, Palace Counselor, and Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 宿衛謹敕，爵位益尊，節操愈謙，散輿馬、衣裘振施賓客，家無所餘；

translations.literal: On night guard he was careful and restrained; as rank grew more honored, his conduct became more humble; he scattered carriages, horses, and fur coats to relieve and bestow on guests—at home nothing remained;
translations.idiomatic: On night guard he was careful and restrained; as rank grew more honored, his conduct became more humble; he scattered carriages, horses, and fur coats to relieve and bestow on guests—at home nothing remained;

sentences.zh: 收贍名士，交結將、相、卿、大夫甚眾。

translations.literal: he gathered and sustained famous scholars and formed ties with many generals, chancellors, ministers, and grandees.
translations.idiomatic: he gathered and sustained famous scholars and formed ties with many generals, chancellors, ministers, and grandees.

sentences.zh: 故在位更推薦之，游者為之談說，虛譽隆洽，傾其諸父矣。

translations.literal: Therefore those in office further recommended him; wanderers spoke for him; empty praise rose and spread, overwhelming his various uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those in office further recommended him; wanderers spoke for him; empty praise rose and spread, overwhelming his various uncles.

sentences.zh: 敢為激發之行，處之不漸恧。

translations.literal: He dared perform stirring and arousing acts and, placed in them, was not gradually ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: He dared perform stirring and arousing acts and, placed in them, was not gradually ashamed.

sentences.zh: 嘗私買侍婢，昆弟或頗聞知，莽因曰：「後將軍朱子元無子，莽聞此兒種宜子，為買之」。

translations.literal: Once he privately bought a palace maid; brothers perhaps somewhat heard and knew; Mang therefore said: "Later General Zhu Ziyuan has no son; Mang heard this child's seed is fit for sons and bought her for him."
translations.idiomatic: Once he privately bought a palace maid; brothers perhaps somewhat heard and knew; Mang therefore said, "Later General Zhu Ziyuan has no son; Mang heard this child's seed is fit for sons and bought her for him."

sentences.zh: 即日以婢奉朱博。

translations.literal: That very day he presented the maid to Zhu Bo.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he presented the maid to Zhu Bo.

sentences.zh: 其匿情求名如此！

translations.literal: His concealing feeling and seeking fame was like this!
translations.idiomatic: His concealing feeling and seeking fame was like this!

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，立皇后趙氏，大赦天下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin, Empress Zhao was established and a great amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin, Empress Zhao was established and a great amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.

sentences.zh: 皇后既立，寵少衰。

translations.literal: After the empress was established, favor somewhat declined.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress was established, favor somewhat declined.

sentences.zh: 而其女弟絕幸，為昭儀，居昭陽捨，其中庭彤朱而殿上髹漆；

translations.literal: Yet her younger sister had absolute favor, was made Brilliant Companion, and dwelt in Zhaoyang Lodge; within, the central court was cinnabar red and the hall above lacquered;
translations.idiomatic: Yet her younger sister had absolute favor, was made Brilliant Companion, and dwelt in Zhaoyang Lodge; within, the central court was cinnabar red and the hall above lacquered;

sentences.zh: 切皆銅沓，黃金塗；

translations.literal: the cuttings all were copper plates, gilded with gold;
translations.idiomatic: the cuttings all were copper plates, gilded with gold;

sentences.zh: 白玉階；

translations.literal: white jade steps;
translations.idiomatic: white jade steps;

sentences.zh: 壁帶往往為黃金釭，函藍田璧、明珠、翠羽飾之。

translations.literal: wall bands here and there were golden sockets, caskets holding Lantian jade disks, bright pearls, and kingfisher feathers to adorn them.
translations.idiomatic: wall bands here and there were golden sockets, caskets holding Lantian jade disks, bright pearls, and kingfisher feathers to adorn them.

sentences.zh: 自後宮未嘗有焉。

translations.literal: Since the inner palace there had never been such.
translations.idiomatic: Since the inner palace there had never been such.

sentences.zh: 趙後居別館，多通侍郎、宮奴多子者。

translations.literal: Empress Zhao dwelt in a separate lodge and frequently connected with Gentlemen of Attendance and palace slaves who had many sons.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhao dwelt in a separate lodge and frequently connected with Gentlemen of Attendance and palace slaves who had many sons.

sentences.zh: 昭儀嘗謂帝曰：「妾姊性剛，有如為人構陷，則趙氏無種矣！

translations.literal: The Brilliant Companion once said to the emperor: "Your concubine's elder sister's nature is hard; if someone frames her, then the Zhao clan will have no seed!
translations.idiomatic: The Brilliant Companion once said to the emperor, "Your concubine's elder sister's nature is hard; if someone frames her, then the Zhao clan will have no seed!

sentences.zh: 」因泣下心妻惻。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she wept, her heart and wife's sorrow moving.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon she wept, her heart and wife's sorrow moving.

sentences.zh: 帝信之，有白後奸狀者，帝輒殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor believed her; whoever reported the empress's licentious conduct, the emperor immediately killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed her; whoever reported the empress's licentious conduct, the emperor immediately killed.

sentences.zh: 由是後公為淫恣，無敢言者，然卒無子。

translations.literal: From this the empress openly was licentious and unrestrained; none dared speak—yet in the end she had no son.
translations.idiomatic: From this the empress openly was licentious and unrestrained; none dared speak—yet in the end she had no son.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫劉向以為王教由內及外，自近者始，於是採取《詩》、《書》所載賢妃、貞婦興國顯家及孽、嬖亂亡者，序次為《列女傳》，凡八篇，及采傳記行事，著《新序》、《說苑》，凡五十篇，奏之，數上疏言得失，陳法戒。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendor Liu Xiang held that royal instruction proceeds from within to without, beginning with those nearest; he thereupon gathered from what the Odes and Documents record—worthy consorts and chaste wives who raised states and glorified families, and wicked and favored women who brought disorder and ruin—arranged them in order as the Biographies of Exemplary Women, eight fascicles in all; and also collected from traditions and recorded conduct, composing the New Arrangements and the Garden of Sayings, fifty fascicles in all, and presented them; he repeatedly submitted memorials stating gain and loss and setting forth laws and warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendor Liu Xiang held that royal instruction proceeds from within outward, beginning with those nearest; he thereupon gathered from the Odes and Documents worthy consorts and chaste wives who raised states and glorified families, and wicked and favored women who brought disorder and ruin, arranged them as the Biographies of Exemplary Women in eight fascicles; he also collected traditions and recorded conduct in the New Arrangements and the Garden of Sayings, fifty fascicles in all, and presented them, repeatedly memorializing on gain and loss and setting forth laws and warnings.

sentences.zh: 書數十上，以助觀覽，補遺闕。

translations.literal: His writings were submitted several tens of times, to assist observation and perusal and to supplement omissions and gaps.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his writings dozens of times to assist the emperor's reading and to fill omissions and gaps.

sentences.zh: 上雖不能盡用，然內嘉其言，常嗟歎之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor could not fully employ them, yet inwardly he praised his words and often sighed in admiration over them.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor could not fully adopt his advice, he inwardly praised his words and often sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 昌陵制度奢泰，久而不成。

translations.literal: The Changling project's regulations were extravagant and excessive; long it remained unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: The Changling tomb project was extravagantly designed and long remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 劉向上疏曰：「臣聞王者必通三統，明天命所授者博，非獨一姓也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that a true king must penetrate the three transmissions, making clear that what Heaven's Mandate confers is broad—not a single surname alone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang submitted a memorial, saying, "Your subject has heard that a true king must comprehend the three transmissions of the Mandate, making clear that what Heaven confers is broad—not a single surname alone.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有不亡之國。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, there has never been a state that did not perish.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, there has never been a state that did not perish.

sentences.zh: 孝文皇帝嘗美石槨之固，張釋之曰：『使其中有可欲，雖錮南山猶有隙。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiao Wen once praised the solidity of a stone outer coffin; Zhang Shizhi said: 'If within it there is something desirable, even if the South Mountain were caged around it there would still be a gap.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once praised the solidity of a stone outer coffin; Zhang Shizhi said, 'If within it there is something desirable, even if caged with the South Mountain there would still be a gap.

sentences.zh: 』夫死者無終極，而國家有廢興，故釋之之言為無窮計也。

translations.literal: ' For the dead have no end, yet states have decline and rise; therefore Shizhi's words were planning for the endless future.
translations.idiomatic: ' For the dead have no end, yet states rise and fall; therefore Shizhi's words were planning for the endless future.

sentences.zh: 孝文寤焉，遂薄葬。

translations.literal: Xiao Wen awoke to it and thereupon had a frugal burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wen awoke to it and thereupon ordered a frugal burial.

sentences.zh: 棺槨之作，自黃帝始。

translations.literal: The making of inner and outer coffins began with the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer coffins began with the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 黃帝、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周公，丘□皆小，葬具甚微；

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou—their mounds □ were all small, burial goods extremely slight;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou—their mounds □ were all small and burial goods extremely slight;

sentences.zh: 其賢臣孝子亦承命順意而薄葬之。

translations.literal: their worthy ministers and filial sons likewise received command and followed intent and buried them frugally.
translations.idiomatic: their worthy ministers and filial sons likewise followed command and intent and buried them frugally.

sentences.zh: 此誠奉安君父忠孝之至也。

translations.literal: This truly is the utmost of loyalty and filial piety in securing peace for lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: This truly is the utmost of loyalty and filial piety in securing peace for lord and father.

sentences.zh: 孔子葬母於防，墳四尺。

translations.literal: Confucius buried his mother at Fang; the mound was four feet.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius buried his mother at Fang with a mound four feet high.

sentences.zh: 延陵季子葬其子，封墳掩坎，其高可隱。

translations.literal: Lord Ji of Yanling buried his son, sealed the mound and covered the pit—its height could be hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Ji of Yanling buried his son, sealed the mound and covered the pit—its height could be concealed.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼孝子而延陵慈父，舜、禹忠臣，周公弟弟，其葬君、親、骨肉皆微薄矣。

translations.literal: Thus Zhong Ni was a filial son and Yanling a loving father; Shun and Yu were loyal ministers; the Duke of Zhou was a younger brother—they buried lords, parents, and kin all most frugally.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Confucius was a filial son and Lord Ji of Yanling a loving father; Shun and Yu were loyal ministers; the Duke of Zhou was a younger brother—they all buried lords, parents, and kin most frugally.

sentences.zh: 非苟為儉，誠便於體也。

translations.literal: It was not done merely for thrift; it truly was convenient for the bodily remains.
translations.idiomatic: It was not done merely for thrift; it truly suited the bodily remains.

sentences.zh: 秦始皇帝葬於驪山之阿，下錮三泉，上崇山墳，水銀為江、海，黃金為鳧、雁，珍寶之臧，機械之變，棺槨之麗，宮館之盛，不可勝原。

translations.literal: The First Emperor of Qin was buried at the slope of Mount Li; below, three springs were caged in; above, a mountain mound was heaped; mercury formed rivers and seas; gold formed ducks and geese; stores of treasures, transformations of mechanisms, splendor of coffins, magnificence of palaces and halls—the sources cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin was buried on the slope of Mount Li; below, three springs were sealed in; above, a mountain mound was heaped; mercury formed rivers and seas, gold formed ducks and geese; treasures, mechanisms, splendid coffins, and magnificent palaces—the list cannot be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 天下苦其役而反之，驪山之作未成，而周章百萬之師至其下矣。

translations.literal: All under Heaven suffered from its corvée and turned against him; the Li Mountain work was not yet finished when Zhou Zhang's army of a million reached below it.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven suffered from the corvée and rebelled; the Mount Li project was not yet finished when armies of a million reached its foot.

sentences.zh: 項籍燔其宮室、營宇，牧兒持火照求亡羊，失火燒其臧槨。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu burned his palaces and encampments; a shepherd boy held a torch seeking a lost sheep and by mischance set fire that burned the treasure coffins.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu burned his palaces and halls; a shepherd boy held a torch seeking a lost sheep and accidentally set fire that burned the treasure coffins.

sentences.zh: 自古至今，葬未有盛如始皇者也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, no burial has been as grand as the First Emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to the present, no burial has been as grand as the First Emperor's.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，外被項籍之災，內離牧豎之禍，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Within several years, outwardly he suffered Xiang Yu's disaster, inwardly he met the shepherd boy's calamity—is it not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Within several years he suffered Xiang Yu's disaster from without and the shepherd boy's calamity from within—is it not pitiable!

sentences.zh: 是故德彌厚者葬彌薄，知愈深者葬愈微。

translations.literal: Therefore the thicker virtue is, the thinner the burial; the deeper knowledge is, the slighter the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the greater the virtue, the thinner the burial; the deeper the wisdom, the slighter the burial.

sentences.zh: 無德寡知，其葬愈厚。

translations.literal: Those without virtue and with little knowledge—their burials grow ever thicker.
translations.idiomatic: Those without virtue and with little knowledge bury ever more lavishly.

sentences.zh: 丘隴彌高，宮廟甚麗，發掘必速。

translations.literal: Mounds and ridges grow ever higher, palaces and temples most splendid—exhumation is sure to come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Mounds grow ever higher and palaces ever more splendid—exhumation is sure to come quickly.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，明暗之效，葬之吉凶，昭然可見矣。

translations.literal: From this to observe it, the effect of brightness and darkness, the good and ill of burial, is clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that the effect of wisdom and folly and the good and ill of burial are plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，躬親節儉，始營初陵，其制約小，天下莫不稱賢明；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty took the throne, you personally practiced thrift; when you first planned the initial tomb, its design was restrained and small—all under Heaven none failed to call you worthy and wise;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty took the throne, you personally practiced thrift; when you first planned the initial tomb, its design was modest, and all under Heaven praised your wisdom;

sentences.zh: 及徙昌陵，增卑為高，積土為山，發民墳墓，積以萬數，營起邑居，期日迫卒，功費大萬百餘，死者恨於下，生者愁於上，臣甚愍焉！

translations.literal: but when you moved to Changling, you raised what was low into what was high, heaped earth into mountains, opened the people's graves in numbers accumulated to tens of thousands, built up towns and dwellings, deadlines pressed and rushed, labor costs more than a hundred million— the dead resent below, the living grieve above; your subject is deeply pained!
translations.idiomatic: but when you moved to Changling, you raised what was low into heights, heaped earth into mountains, opened commoners' graves by the tens of thousands, built towns and dwellings, pressed deadlines, spent more than a hundred million in labor—the dead resent below, the living grieve above; your subject is deeply pained!

sentences.zh: 以死者為有知，發人之墓，其害多矣；

translations.literal: If the dead have knowledge, to open people's tombs—its harms are many;
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have knowledge, opening people's tombs does great harm;

sentences.zh: 若其無知，又安用大！

translations.literal: if they have no knowledge, why use such great effort!
translations.idiomatic: if they have no knowledge, why use such great effort!

sentences.zh: 謀之賢知則不說，以示眾庶則苦之，若苟以說愚夫淫侈之人，又何為哉！

translations.literal: To consult the worthy and wise brings no approval; to display it to the masses makes them suffer—if you merely wish to please foolish men and extravagant people, what is the point!
translations.idiomatic: The worthy and wise will not approve; the masses will suffer by it—if you merely wish to please foolish and extravagant men, what is the point!

sentences.zh: 唯陛下上覽明聖之制以為則，下觀亡秦之禍以為戒，初陵之模，宜從公卿大臣之議，以息眾庶！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty above look to the enlightened and sagely institutions as your standard, below observe the calamity of perished Qin as your warning—the model of the initial tomb ought to follow the counsel of grandees and great ministers, to give rest to the masses!
