translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty above take enlightened institutions as your standard and below take perished Qin's calamity as your warning—the initial tomb's design ought to follow the grandees' counsel and give rest to the people!

sentences.zh: 」上感其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor was moved by his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was moved by his words.

sentences.zh: 初，解萬年自詭昌陵三年可成，卒不能就；

translations.literal: Earlier, Jie Wannian himself claimed Changling could be completed in three years, yet in the end it could not be finished;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jie Wannian himself claimed Changling could be finished in three years, yet in the end it could not be completed;

sentences.zh: 群臣多言其不便者。

translations.literal: many among the ministers spoke of its inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: many ministers spoke of its drawbacks.

sentences.zh: 下有司議，皆曰：「昌陵因卑為高，度便房猶在平地上；

translations.literal: It was sent down to the responsible offices for deliberation; all said: "Changling raises what is low into high; measured, the side chambers are still on level ground;
translations.idiomatic: It was sent to the responsible offices for deliberation; all said, "Changling raises what is low into heights; measured, the side chambers are still on level ground;

sentences.zh: 客土之中，不保幽冥之靈，淺外不固。

translations.literal: within borrowed earth, the spirit in the dark netherworld is not secured; shallow and outward, it is not firm.
translations.idiomatic: within borrowed earth the spirit in the netherworld is not secured; shallow and outward, it is not firm.

sentences.zh: 卒徒工庸以巨萬數，至然脂火夜作，取土東山，且與谷同賈，作治數年，天下遍被其勞。

translations.literal: Corvée laborers and hired workers number in the tens of thousands; they even burn grease for lamps and work at night, taking earth from the eastern hills until it costs the same as grain; construction for several years—the whole realm everywhere bears its toil.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée laborers number in the tens of thousands; they even burn lamps and work at night, taking earth from the eastern hills until it costs as much as grain; after years of construction the whole realm bears its toil.

sentences.zh: 故陵因天性，據真土，處勢高敞，旁近祖考，前又已有十年功緒，宜還復故陵，勿徙民，便！

translations.literal: Therefore the tomb should follow Heaven's nature, rest on true earth, occupy a position high and open, lie close to ancestors and forefathers, and before this already had ten years of work begun—it is fitting to return to the former tomb and not move the people—convenient!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the tomb should follow natural terrain, rest on native earth, occupy a high and open site near the ancestors, and ten years of work had already begun on the former site—it is fitting to return to the original tomb and not move the people—best!

sentences.zh: 」秋，七月，詔曰：「朕執德不固，謀不盡下，過聽將作大匠萬年言『昌陵三年可成』，作治五年，中陵、司馬殿門內尚未加功。

translations.literal: " In autumn, the seventh month, an edict said: "We hold to virtue without firmness, our plans do not fully reach below, and wrongly listened to the Master of Works Jie Wannian's words 'Changling can be completed in three years'—construction for five years, yet within the central tomb and the Sima Hall gate inner works labor has not yet been added.
translations.idiomatic: " In autumn, the seventh month, an edict said, "We have held to virtue without firmness, our plans have not fully reached below, and wrongly listened to Master of Works Jie Wannian's claim that 'Changling can be finished in three years'—after five years of construction, work within the central tomb and the Sima Hall gate has not yet been added.

sentences.zh: 天下虛耗，百姓罷勞，客土疏惡，終不可成，朕惟其難，怛然傷心。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is drained empty, the people exhausted with labor; the borrowed earth is loose and poor and ultimately cannot be completed—we think on its difficulty and are suddenly wounded at heart.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven is drained, the people exhausted; the borrowed earth is loose and poor and ultimately cannot succeed—we ponder the difficulty and are suddenly grieved at heart.

sentences.zh: 夫『過而不改，是謂過矣』。

translations.literal: For 'to err and not correct it is called erring still.'
translations.idiomatic: For 'to err and not correct it is still to err.'

sentences.zh: 其罷昌陵，及故陵勿徙吏民，令天下毋有動搖之心。

translations.literal: Let Changling be stopped, and as for the former tomb do not move officials and people, so that all under Heaven has no heart of disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Let Changling be abandoned, and do not move officials and people for the former tomb, so that all under Heaven has no heart of unrest.

sentences.zh: 初，酇侯蕭何之子孫嗣為侯者，無子及有罪，凡五絕祀。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the descendants of Marquis Xiao He of Zan who succeeded as marquises, those without sons and those guilty—in all five times the sacrifices were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, among Marquis Xiao He of Zan's descendants who succeeded as marquises, lines without heirs and lines ended for crimes—in all the sacrifices were cut off five times.

sentences.zh: 高後、文帝、景帝、武帝、宣帝思何之功，輒以其支庶紹封。

translations.literal: Empress Gao, Emperor Wen, Emperor Jing, Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan, mindful of He's merit, each time enfeoffed a collateral branch to continue the line.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Gao, Emperors Wen, Jing, Wu, and Xuan, mindful of He's merit, each time enfeoffed a collateral branch to continue the line.

sentences.zh: 是歲，何七世孫酇侯獲坐使奴殺人，減死，完為城旦。

translations.literal: That year, He's seventh-generation descendant Marquis Huo of Zan was convicted of making a slave kill a man; his death sentence was reduced and he was made a corvée convict.
translations.idiomatic: That year, He's seventh-generation descendant Marquis Huo of Zan was convicted of having a slave kill a man; his death sentence was reduced and he was sentenced to corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 先是，上詔有司訪求漢初功臣之後，久未省錄。

translations.literal: Before this, the emperor had ordered the responsible offices to seek out descendants of the founding Han meritocrats, but long they had not been entered in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the emperor had ordered the responsible offices to seek descendants of Han's founding meritocrats, but long they had not been registered.

sentences.zh: 杜業說上曰：「唐、虞、三代皆封建諸侯，以成太平之美，是以燕、齊之祀與周並傳，子繼弟及，歷載不墮。

translations.literal: Du Ye urged the emperor, saying: "Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all enfeoffed feudal lords to complete the beauty of great peace; therefore the sacrifices of Yan and Qi were transmitted together with Zhou—sons succeeding, younger brothers following—and through the ages did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ye urged the emperor, saying, "Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all enfeoffed feudal lords to achieve great peace; therefore the sacrifices of Yan and Qi were transmitted with Zhou—sons succeeding and younger brothers following—and through the ages did not fall.

sentences.zh: 豈無刑辟、繇祖之竭力，故支庶賴焉。

translations.literal: How could it be without punishments and the ancestors' full effort—therefore collateral lines relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: This was not without punishments and the ancestors' full effort, so collateral lines could rely on it.

sentences.zh: 跡漢功臣，亦皆割符世爵，受山河之誓；

translations.literal: Tracing Han's meritocrats, they too all received split tallies and hereditary enfeoffments and took oaths of mountains and rivers;
translations.idiomatic: Tracing Han's meritocrats, they too all received split tallies, hereditary enfeoffments, and oaths over mountains and rivers;

sentences.zh: 百餘年間，而襲封者盡，朽骨孤於墓，苗裔流於道，生為愍隸，死為轉屍。

translations.literal: within a hundred-odd years those who inherited enfeoffment were exhausted; rotten bones lay lonely in tombs, descendants drifted on the roads—alive they were pitying bondsmen, dead they were corpses passed along.
translations.idiomatic: within a hundred-odd years those who inherited enfeoffment were gone; bones lay lonely in tombs and descendants drifted on the roads—alive they were wretched bondsmen, dead they were corpses cast aside.

sentences.zh: 以往況今，甚可悲傷。

translations.literal: Using the past to measure the present—it is deeply pitiable and wounding.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring the present by the past is deeply pitiable.

sentences.zh: 聖朝憐閔，詔求其後，四方忻忻，靡不歸心。

translations.literal: The sagely court took pity, issued an edict to seek their descendants, and the four quarters were joyful—none failed to turn their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The sagely court took pity and issued an edict to seek their descendants; the four quarters rejoiced and all turned their hearts.

sentences.zh: 出入數年而不省察，恐議者不思大義，徒設虛言，則厚德掩息，吝簡布章，非所以示化勸後也。

translations.literal: Several years have passed in and out without examination—I fear deliberators do not think on great righteousness but merely set up empty words; then thick virtue is covered and stilled, stinginess and brevity spread their chapters—not the means to display transformation and encourage posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Several years have passed without examination—I fear deliberators do not consider great righteousness but merely set up empty words; then thick virtue is stifled and stinginess spreads its chapters—not the way to display transformation and encourage posterity.

sentences.zh: 雖難盡繼，宜從尤功。

translations.literal: Although it is hard to continue them all completely, one ought to follow those of greatest merit.
translations.idiomatic: Although it is hard to continue them all, one ought to begin with those of greatest merit.

sentences.zh: 」上納其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，封蕭何六世孫南□長喜為酇侯。

translations.literal: On guimao, he enfeoffed Xiao He's sixth-generation descendant Chief Xi of Nan □ as Marquis of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, he enfeoffed Xiao He's sixth-generation descendant Chief Xi of Nan □ as Marquis of Zan.

sentences.zh: 立城陽哀王弟俚為王。

translations.literal: He installed the younger brother of King Ai of Chengyang, Li, as king.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Li, younger brother of King Ai of Chengyang, as king.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁丑，太皇太后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingchou, Grand Empress Dowager Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingchou, Grand Empress Dowager Wang died.

sentences.zh: 九月，黑龍見東萊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, a black dragon appeared in Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, a black dragon appeared in Donglai.

sentences.zh: 丁巳晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the cycle, dingsi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以南陽太守陳咸為少府，侍中淳于長為水衡都尉。

translations.literal: That year, Chen Xian, Administrator of Nanyang, was made Minister Steward; Attendant-in-Ordinary Chunyu Chang was made Commandant of the Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Chen Xian, Administrator of Nanyang, was made Minister Steward, and Attendant-in-Ordinary Chunyu Chang was made Commandant of the Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己丑，安陽敬侯王音薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jichou, Marquis Jing of Anyang Wang Yin died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jichou, Marquis Jing of Anyang Wang Yin died.

sentences.zh: 王氏唯音為修整，數諫正，有忠直節。

translations.literal: Of the Wang clan only Yin was well ordered; he repeatedly remonstrated and corrected and had a loyal and upright integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Wang clan only Yin was well ordered; he repeatedly remonstrated and had loyal, upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未夜，星隕如雨，繹繹，未至地滅。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the night of guiwei, stars fell like rain, streaming and streaming, and were extinguished before reaching the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the night of guiwei, stars fell like rain in streams and were extinguished before reaching the ground.

sentences.zh: 乙酉晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the cycle, yiyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉，以成都侯王商為大司馬、衛將軍；

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingyou, Marquis of Chengdu Wang Shang was made Grand Marshal and Defender-General;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingyou, Marquis of Chengdu Wang Shang was made Grand Marshal and Defender-General;

sentences.zh: 紅陽侯王立位特進，領城門兵。

translations.literal: Marquis of Hongyang Wang Li was given the special advancement rank and commanded the gate-guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Hongyang Wang Li was given special advancement rank and commanded the gate-guard troops.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹翟方進為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Magistrate Zhai Fangjin was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Magistrate Zhai Fangjin was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 谷永為涼州刺史，奏事京師，訖，當之部，上使尚書問永，受所欲言。

translations.literal: Gu Yong was Regional Inspector of Liangzhou; he memorialized at the capital, and when finished, as he was about to go to his post, the emperor sent the Master of Documents to ask Yong to receive whatever he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong was Regional Inspector of Liangzhou; after memorializing at the capital, as he was about to depart for his post, the emperor sent the Master of Documents to ask Yong to say whatever he wished.

sentences.zh: 永對曰：「臣聞王天下、有國家者，患在上有危亡之事而危亡之言不得上聞。

translations.literal: Yong replied, saying: "Your subject has heard that one who rules all under Heaven and holds a state—the worry is that above there are matters of peril and ruin yet words of peril and ruin cannot be heard above.
translations.idiomatic: Yong replied, saying, "Your subject has heard that one who rules all under Heaven and holds a state fears that above there are matters of peril and ruin yet words of peril and ruin cannot reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 如使危亡之言輒上聞，則商、周不易姓而迭興，三正不變改而更用。

translations.literal: If words of peril and ruin were at once heard above, then Shang and Zhou would not have changed surnames yet risen in succession, and the three orthodoxies would not have changed and been used anew.
translations.idiomatic: If words of peril and ruin reached the throne at once, Shang and Zhou would not have changed surnames yet risen in succession, and the three orthodoxies would not have changed and been renewed.

sentences.zh: 夏、商之將亡也，行道之人皆知之。

translations.literal: When Xia and Shang were about to perish, travelers on the road all knew it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia and Shang were about to perish, travelers on the road all knew it.

sentences.zh: 晏然自以若天有日，莫能危，是故惡日廣而不自知，大命傾而不自寤。

translations.literal: They were tranquil and took themselves as if Heaven had a sun—none could endanger them; therefore evil grew daily without their knowing it, the great mandate tilted without their awakening.
translations.idiomatic: They were tranquil, thinking that as Heaven has a sun none could endanger them; therefore evil grew daily without their knowing it and the great mandate tilted without their awakening.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『危者有其安者也，亡者保其存者也。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'Where there is peril, there is that which secures safety; where there is ruin, there is that which preserves existence.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'Where there is peril, there is that which secures safety; where there is ruin, there is that which preserves existence.

sentences.zh: 』陛下誠垂寬明之聽，無忌諱之誅，使芻蕘之臣得盡所聞於前，群臣之上願，社稷之長福也！

translations.literal: ' If Your Majesty truly extends a broad and clear hearing, without punishments for taboo subjects, so that grass-and-firewood subjects may fully state what they have heard before you—the upper wish of your ministers, the long blessing of the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: ' If Your Majesty truly extends a broad and clear hearing, without punishing taboo subjects, so that humble subjects may fully state what they have heard before you—that is your ministers' highest wish and the altars' lasting blessing!

sentences.zh: 元年，九月，黑龍見；

translations.literal: In the first year, the ninth month, a black dragon appeared;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year, the ninth month, a black dragon appeared;

sentences.zh: 其晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: on its last day, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: on its last day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 今年二月己未夜，星隕；

translations.literal: This year, on the night of jiwei in the second month, stars fell;
translations.idiomatic: This year, on the night of jiwei in the second month, stars fell;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，日有食之。

translations.literal: on yiyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: on yiyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 六月之間，大異四發，二二而同月。

translations.literal: Within the sixth month, great anomalies issued four times—two and two in the same month.
translations.idiomatic: Within the sixth month, four great anomalies occurred—two pairs in the same month.

sentences.zh: 三代之末，春秋之亂，未嘗有也。

translations.literal: At the ends of the Three Dynasties, in the chaos of the Spring and Autumn, there never were such.
translations.idiomatic: At the ends of the Three Dynasties and in the chaos of the Spring and Autumn, there never were such.

sentences.zh: 臣聞三代所以隕社稷、喪宗廟者，皆由婦人與群惡沉湎於酒；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that what made the Three Dynasties fall in altars of soil and grain and lose ancestral temples was all through women and a host of villains steeped in wine;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the Three Dynasties lost their altars and ancestral temples all through women and villains steeped in wine;

sentences.zh: 秦所以二世十六年而亡者，養生泰奢，奉終泰厚也。

translations.literal: what made Qin perish in the sixteenth year of the Second Emperor was nourishing life most extravagant and serving the end most thick.
translations.idiomatic: what made Qin perish in the Second Emperor's sixteenth year was extravagant living and lavish burial.

sentences.zh: 二者，陛下兼而有之，臣請略陳其效。

translations.literal: Both of these Your Majesty combines in having; your subject requests briefly to set forth their effects.
translations.idiomatic: Both of these Your Majesty combines; your subject requests briefly to set forth their effects.

sentences.zh: 「建始、河平之際，許、班之貴，傾動前朝，熏灼四方，女寵至極，不可上矣；

translations.literal: " At the time of Jianshi and Heping, the nobility of the Xu and Ban clans shook the former court and scorched the four quarters; favor to women reached the utmost—it could not go higher;
translations.idiomatic: " At the time of Jianshi and Heping, the Xu and Ban clans' nobility shook the former court and scorched the four quarters; favor to women reached its peak—it could go no higher;

sentences.zh: 今之後起，什倍於前。

translations.literal: what rises now is tenfold the former.
translations.idiomatic: what has risen since is tenfold the former.

sentences.zh: 廢先帝法度，聽用其言，官秩不當，縱釋王誅，驕其親屬，假之威權，從橫亂政，刺舉之吏莫敢奉憲。

translations.literal: They abolish the former emperor's laws and institutions, listen to and employ their words, offices and ranks are improper, they release and pardon those the king should execute, make arrogant their kin, lend them authority and power, and with unchecked license disorder government—investigating officers dare not uphold the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: They abolish the former emperor's laws, heed their words, grant improper offices and ranks, release those the king should execute, indulge their kin, lend them authority, and with unchecked license disorder government—investigating officers dare not uphold the statutes.

sentences.zh: 又以掖庭獄大為亂阱，榜棰憯於砲烙，絕滅人命，主為趙、李報德復怨。

translations.literal: They also make the Lateral Court prison a great trap of disorder—flogging and beating more cruel than the cannonade—cutting off human lives, mainly to repay kindness and settle grudges for Zhao and Li.
translations.idiomatic: They also make the Lateral Court prison a great trap—flogging more cruel than the cannonade—destroying lives mainly to repay kindness and settle grudges for Zhao and Li.

sentences.zh: 反除白罪，建治正吏，多繫無辜，掠立迫恐，至為人起責，分利受謝，生入死出者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: They reverse and remove proven guilt, establish prosecutions against upright officials, imprison many innocents, extort and set up coercion and terror, even incurring debts for others, sharing profit and receiving bribes—those who enter alive and leave dead cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: They reverse proven guilt, prosecute upright officials, imprison many innocents, extort and terrorize, even incur debts for others and share profits and bribes—those who enter alive and leave dead cannot be counted.

sentences.zh: 是以日食再既，以昭其辜。

translations.literal: Therefore solar eclipses twice reached totality, to display their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore solar eclipses twice reached totality, to display their guilt.

sentences.zh: 「王者必先自絕，然後天絕之。

translations.literal: " A true king must first cut himself off, and only then does Heaven cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: " A true king must first cut himself off, and only then does Heaven cut him off.

sentences.zh: 今陛下棄萬乘之至貴，樂家人之賤事，厭高美之尊號，好匹夫之卑字，崇聚僄輕無義小人以為私客，數離深宮之固，挺身晨夜，與群小相隨，烏集雜會，飲醉吏民之家，亂服共坐，流湎媟嫚，溷淆無別，黽勉遁樂，晝夜在路，典門戶、奉宿衛之臣執干戈而守空宮，公卿百僚不知陛下所在，積數年矣。

translations.literal: " Now Your Majesty abandons the utmost nobility of ten thousand chariots, delights in the base affairs of a household, is weary of high and beautiful honorific titles, loves the low pet-names of common men, honors and gathers flighty, light, and unrighteous petty men as private guests, repeatedly leaves the secure deep palace, thrusts his person forth morning and night, follows with a host of petty men, gathers like crows in mixed assemblies, drinks drunk in officials' and commoners' houses, sits in disorderly dress together, flows deep in lewd familiarity, muddles and mixes without distinction, strives in flight to pleasure, day and night on the roads—the officers who manage gates and households and perform night guard hold weapons and guard an empty palace; grandees and the hundred officials do not know where Your Majesty is—this has accumulated for several years.
translations.idiomatic: " Now Your Majesty abandons the nobility of ten thousand chariots, delights in household trifles, wearies of lofty titles, loves common men's nicknames, honors and gathers flighty, unrighteous petty men as private guests, repeatedly leaves the secure deep palace, goes forth morning and night with petty followers, gathers like crows in mixed assemblies, drinks drunk in officials' and commoners' houses, sits in disorderly dress, flows deep in lewd familiarity without distinction, strives in flight to pleasure day and night on the roads—officers who manage gates and night guard hold weapons and guard an empty palace; grandees and officials do not know where Your Majesty is—this has gone on for years.

sentences.zh: 「王者以民為基，民以財為本，財竭則下畔，下畔則上亡。

translations.literal: " A true king takes the people as his foundation; the people take wealth as their root—when wealth is exhausted those below rebel, when those below rebel those above perish.
translations.idiomatic: " A true king takes the people as his foundation; the people take wealth as their root—when wealth is exhausted the people rebel, and when the people rebel the ruler perishes.

sentences.zh: 是以明王愛養基本，不敢窮極，使民如承大祭。

translations.literal: Therefore enlightened kings cherish and nourish the foundation and dare not exhaust it to the limit, making the people as if undertaking a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore enlightened kings cherish and nourish the foundation and dare not exhaust it, treating the people as if undertaking a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今陛下輕奪民財，不愛民力，聽邪臣之計，去高敞初陵，改作昌陵，役百乾溪，費擬驪山，靡敝天下，五年不成而後反故。

translations.literal: " Now Your Majesty lightly seizes the people's wealth, does not cherish the people's strength, listens to wicked ministers' plans, leaves the high and open initial tomb, and changes construction to Changling—corvée like a hundred Qianxi, expense rivaling Mount Li, wasting and wearing out all under Heaven; five years it was not finished and only then you returned to the former site.
translations.idiomatic: " Now Your Majesty lightly seizes the people's wealth, does not cherish their strength, listens to wicked ministers' plans, leaves the high and open initial tomb for Changling—corvée like a hundred Qianxi, expense rivaling Mount Li, wasting all under Heaven; after five years it was unfinished and only then you returned to the former site.

sentences.zh: 百姓愁恨感天，饑饉仍臻，流散冗食，餧死於道，以百萬數。

translations.literal: The people grieve and resent and move Heaven; famine follows in succession; they drift scattered and eat as refugees; starve to death on the roads—in numbers of a million.
translations.idiomatic: The people grieve and resent and move Heaven; famine follows; they drift scattered as refugees and starve on the roads by the millions.

sentences.zh: 公家無一年之畜，百姓無旬日之儲，上下俱匱，無以相救。

translations.literal: The public household has not a year's store; the people have not a ten-day's reserve; above and below are together depleted—there is no means to rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: The public treasury has not a year's store; the people have not ten days' reserve; above and below are together depleted with no means to rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『殷鑒不遠，在夏后之世。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Yin's mirror is not far—it is in the age of the lord of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, 'Yin's mirror is not far—it is in the age of the lord of Xia.

sentences.zh: 』願陛下追觀夏、商、周、秦所以失之，以鏡考己行，有不合者，臣當伏妄言之誅！

translations.literal: ' We wish Your Majesty to trace back and observe how Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Qin lost their way, to take a mirror and examine your own conduct—where it does not accord, your subject ought to submit to punishment for reckless speech!
translations.idiomatic: ' May Your Majesty trace how Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Qin lost their way, take a mirror to examine your own conduct—where it does not accord, your subject will submit to punishment for reckless speech!

sentences.zh: 「漢興九世，百九十餘載，繼體之主七，皆承天順道，遵先祖法度，或以中興，或以治安；

translations.literal: "Since Han arose, nine generations and more than one hundred ninety years have passed; seven lords who succeeded the line all received Heaven and followed the Way, observed the ancestral laws and standards, some achieving restoration, some achieving order and peace;
translations.idiomatic: "Since Han arose there have been nine generations and more than one hundred ninety years; seven succession emperors all received Heaven's mandate and followed the Way, observed ancestral law, and achieved either restoration or peace and order;

sentences.zh: 至於陛下，獨違道縱欲，輕身妄行，當盛壯之隆，無繼嗣之福，有危亡之憂，積失君道，不合天意，亦以多矣。

translations.literal: as for Your Majesty, alone you violate the Way and indulge desires, treat your person lightly and act recklessly; at the height of vigorous prime you lack the blessing of an heir, bear the worry of peril and ruin, accumulate failures of the lord's Way, and do not accord with Heaven's intent—these too are already many.
translations.idiomatic: yet Your Majesty alone violates the Way and indulges desire, treats your person lightly and acts recklessly; in the prime of vigorous youth you lack the blessing of an heir and bear the worry of peril and ruin. Failures of kingship that do not accord with Heaven's intent are already many.

sentences.zh: 為人後嗣，守人功業如此，豈不負哉！

translations.literal: As another's successor, to guard another's achievement and enterprise in this way—how is it not a betrayal!
translations.idiomatic: As successor to another's line, to guard their achievement in this way—how is that not a betrayal!

sentences.zh: 方今社稷、宗廟禍福、安危之機在於陛下，陛下誠肯昭然遠寤，專心反道，舊愆畢改，新德既章，則赫赫大異庶幾可銷，天命去就庶幾可復，社稷、宗廟庶幾可保！

translations.literal: Now the turning point of blessing and calamity, safety and peril for the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple lies with Your Majesty. If Your Majesty truly will clearly awaken from afar, single-mindedly return to the Way, completely change old faults, and make new virtue manifest, then the glaring great anomalies may perhaps be dispelled, Heaven's mandate of departure and return may perhaps be restored, and the altars of soil and grain and ancestral temple may perhaps be preserved!
translations.idiomatic: Now whether the altars of state and ancestral temple meet blessing or calamity, safety or peril, turns on Your Majesty. If Your Majesty will truly awaken clearly, single-mindedly return to the Way, wholly amend old faults, and make new virtue manifest, then glaring portents may perhaps be dispelled, Heaven's mandate may perhaps be restored, and state and ancestral temple may perhaps be preserved!

sentences.zh: 唯陛下留神反覆，熟省臣言！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty keep your spirit and reflect repeatedly, and carefully consider my words!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty reflect repeatedly and carefully consider my words!

sentences.zh: 帝性寬，好文辭，而溺於燕樂，皆皇太后與諸舅夙夜所常憂；

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was lenient; he loved literary compositions, yet was drowned in feasting and music—all matters the Empress Dowager and the various maternal uncles worried over day and night;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was lenient by nature and loved literary composition, yet was sunk in feasting and music—matters the Empress Dowager and his maternal uncles worried over day and night;

sentences.zh: 至親難數言，故推永等使因天變而切諫，勸上納用之。

translations.literal: close kin find it hard to speak repeatedly, so they pushed Yong and others to use heaven's changes for stern remonstrance and urge the emperor to accept and employ it.
translations.idiomatic: close kin find it hard to speak frankly and often, so they urged Yong and others to seize heaven's warnings for stern remonstrance and persuade the emperor to heed them.

sentences.zh: 永自知有內應，展意無所依違，每言事輒見答禮。

translations.literal: Yong himself knew he had support within; he could unfold his intent without yielding, and whenever he spoke on affairs he was always answered with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yong knew he had backers within the palace; he could speak his mind without holding back, and whenever he addressed affairs the emperor answered him courteously.

sentences.zh: 至上此對，上大怒。

translations.literal: When he submitted this response, the emperor was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted this memorial, the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍商密擿永令發去。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Shang secretly denounced Yong and had him sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Wang Shang secretly denounced Yong and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上使侍御史收永，敕過交道廄者勿追；

translations.literal: The emperor sent the attendant censor to seize Yong and ordered that those past the Jiaodao stable should not pursue;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the attendant censor to seize Yong and ordered that pursuers should not go past the Jiaodao stable;

sentences.zh: 御史不及永，還。

translations.literal: the censor did not overtake Yong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: the censor did not overtake Yong and returned.

sentences.zh: 上意亦解，自悔。

translations.literal: The emperor's mood also eased, and he regretted it himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased and he regretted his action.

sentences.zh: 上嘗與張放及趙、李諸侍中共宴飲禁中，皆引滿舉白，談笑大噱。

translations.literal: The emperor once feasted and drank in the inner palace with Zhang Fang and the various attendants Zhao and Li; all filled their cups and raised them to drain, talking and laughing with loud guffaws.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once feasted in the inner palace with Zhang Fang and attendants Zhao, Li, and others; all filled their cups and drained them together, talking and laughing loudly.

sentences.zh: 時乘輿幄坐張畫屏風，畫紂醉踞妲己，作長夜之樂。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage's curtained seat had a painted screen spread out, depicting Zhou drunken and sprawling on Daji, making the music of the long night.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage's curtained seat had a painted screen spread out, showing King Zhou drunk and sprawling on Daji amid the revelry of the long night.

sentences.zh: 侍中、光祿大夫班伯久疾新起，上顧指畫而問伯曰：「紂為無道，至於是虖？

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Household Grandee Ban Bo, long ill and newly risen, the emperor turned, pointed at the painting, and asked Bo, saying: "Zhou was without the Way—did it reach this?
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant and Household Grandee Ban Bo, long ill and newly recovered, was present. The emperor turned, pointed at the painting, and asked Bo, "King Zhou was utterly wicked—did it really come to this?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「《書》云：『乃用婦人之言』，何有踞肆於朝！

translations.literal: " He replied, saying: "The Documents says: 'Then he used the woman's words'—how could there be sprawling insolence in court!
translations.idiomatic: " Bo replied, "The Documents says, 'Then he used the woman's words'—how could there be such sprawling insolence at court!

sentences.zh: 所謂眾惡歸之，不如是之甚者也！

translations.literal: What is called 'all evils converge on him' is not as extreme as this!
translations.idiomatic: What people mean when they say all evils converged on him was not as extreme as this!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「苟不若此，此圖何戒？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If it were not like this, what warning would this picture hold?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If it were not like that, what warning would this picture hold?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「『沉湎於酒』，微子所以告去也。

translations.literal: " He replied, saying: "'Sunk deep in wine'—that is why Weizi announced his departure.
translations.idiomatic: " Bo replied, "'Sunk deep in wine'—that is why Weizi announced his departure.

sentences.zh: 『式號式呼』，《大雅》所以流連也。

translations.literal: 'Shouting and calling'—that is why the Greater Odes laments lingering excess.
translations.idiomatic: 'Shouting and calling'—that is what the Greater Odes laments as lingering debauchery.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《書》淫亂之戒，其原皆在於酒！

translations.literal: The warnings of licentious disorder in the Odes and Documents—all their sources lie in wine!
translations.idiomatic: The Odes and Documents warn against licentious disorder, and the root of it all is wine!

sentences.zh: 」上乃喟然歎曰：「吾久不見班生，今日復聞讜言！

translations.literal: " The emperor then sighed and said: "I have long not seen Master Ban; today I again hear straightforward words!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed and said, "I have long not seen Master Ban; today I again hear honest counsel!

sentences.zh: 」放等不懌，稍自引起更衣，因罷出。

translations.literal: " Fang and the others were displeased, gradually rose on the pretext of changing clothes, and thus withdrew when the feast ended.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang and the others were displeased, rose on the pretext of changing clothes, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時長信庭林表適使來，聞見之。

translations.literal: At the time Lin Biao, envoy from Changxin Hall, happened to have come and heard and saw it.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Biao, an envoy from Changxin Hall, happened to be present and witnessed it.

sentences.zh: 後上朝東宮，太后泣曰：「帝間顏色瘦黑。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor attended at the Eastern Palace, the Empress Dowager wept and said: "Between audiences Your Majesty's complexion is thin and dark.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor attended at the Eastern Palace, the Empress Dowager wept and said, "Between audiences your complexion is thin and dark.

sentences.zh: 班侍中本大將軍所舉，宜寵異之；

translations.literal: Attendant Ban was originally recommended by the Grand General; he should be favored exceptionally;
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Ban was originally recommended by the Grand General; you should favor him exceptionally;

sentences.zh: 益求其比，以輔聖德！

translations.literal: seek more like him to assist sagely virtue!
translations.idiomatic: seek more like him to assist your sagely virtue!

sentences.zh: 宜遣富平侯且就國！

translations.literal: You should send the Marquis of Fuping back to his fief for the time being!
translations.idiomatic: You should send the Marquis of Fuping back to his fief for now!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Very well.

sentences.zh: 」上諸舅聞之，以風丞相、御史，求放過失。

translations.literal: " The emperor's various maternal uncles heard of it and hinted to the chancellor and censor to seek Fang's faults.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's maternal uncles heard of it and hinted to the chancellor and censor to seek Zhang Fang's faults.

sentences.zh: 於是丞相宣、御史大夫方進奏「放驕蹇縱恣，奢淫不制，拒閉使者，賊傷無辜，從者支屬並乘權勢，為暴虐，請免放就國。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chancellor Xuan and Censor-in-Chief Fangjin memorialized, "Fang is arrogant, obstinate, and unrestrained, extravagant and licentious without limit, repelled and shut out envoys, robbed and harmed the innocent, and his followers and collateral kin all rode on power to commit violence and cruelty. We request that Fang be dismissed and sent to his fief."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chancellor Xuan and Censor-in-Chief Fangjin memorialized that Zhang Fang was arrogant, unrestrained, extravagant and licentious beyond measure, had repelled imperial envoys, robbed and harmed innocents, and his followers and kin had abused power with violence and cruelty. They requested that Fang be dismissed and sent to his fief.

sentences.zh: 」上不得已，左遷放為北地都尉。

translations.literal: " The emperor had no choice and demoted Fang to be commandant of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor had no choice and demoted Fang to commandant of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 其後比年數有災變，故放久不得還。

translations.literal: Afterward, for several years in succession there were disasters and anomalies, so Fang long could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward disasters and portents occurred several years in succession, so Fang long could not return.

sentences.zh: 璽書勞問不絕。

translations.literal: Imperial letters of consolation and inquiry never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters of consolation and inquiry never ceased.

sentences.zh: 敬武公主有疾，詔徽放歸第視母疾。

translations.literal: Princess Jingwu fell ill; an edict recalled Fang to his residence to attend his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jingwu fell ill; an edict recalled Fang to his residence to tend his mother's illness.

sentences.zh: 數月，主有瘳，後復出放為河東都尉。

translations.literal: After several months the princess recovered, and later Fang was again sent out as commandant of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After several months the princess recovered, and later Fang was again sent out as commandant of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 上雖愛放，然上迫太后，下用大臣，故常涕泣而遣之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor loved Fang, he was pressed above by the Empress Dowager and employed the great ministers below, and therefore often sent him away with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor loved Fang, he was pressed by the Empress Dowager above and the great ministers below, and therefore often sent him away in tears.

sentences.zh: 邛成太后之崩也，喪事倉卒，吏賦斂以趨辦，上聞之，以過丞相、御史。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Qiongcheng died, the funeral rites were hurried; officials levied exactions to rush completion. When the emperor heard of it, he blamed the chancellor and censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Qiongcheng died, the funeral was rushed and officials levied exactions to finish it in haste. When the emperor heard of this, he blamed the chancellor and censor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己丑，冊免丞相宣為庶人，御史大夫方進左遷執金吾。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on jichou, by patent Xuan was dismissed as chancellor and made a commoner; Censor-in-Chief Fangjin was demoted to Commandant of the Metropolitan Convoy.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jichou, Xuan was dismissed by patent from the chancellorship and reduced to commoner status; Censor-in-Chief Fangjin was demoted to Commandant of the Metropolitan Convoy.

sentences.zh: 二十餘日，丞相官缺，群臣多舉方進者；

translations.literal: After more than twenty days the chancellor's office was vacant; many among the ministers and officials recommended Fangjin;
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days the chancellorship was vacant; many officials recommended Fangjin;

sentences.zh: 上亦器其能，十一月，壬子，擢方進為丞相，封高陵侯。

translations.literal: the emperor also valued his ability. Eleventh month, on renzi, Fangjin was promoted to chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also valued his ability. In the eleventh month, on renzi, Fangjin was promoted to chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 以諸吏、散騎、光祿勳孔光為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Palace, Rapid Cavalryman, and Household Grandee Kong Guang was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Guang, Gentleman-of-the-Palace, Rapid Cavalryman, and Household Grandee, was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 方進以經術進，其為吏，用法刻深，好任勢立威；

translations.literal: Fangjin advanced through classical learning; as an official he applied the law harshly and deeply, loved relying on power to establish authority;
translations.idiomatic: Fangjin had risen through classical learning; as an official he applied the law harshly and loved to rely on power to establish authority;

sentences.zh: 有所忌惡，峻文深詆，中傷甚多。

translations.literal: toward those he resented he used severe statutes and deep slander, wounding many.
translations.idiomatic: toward those he resented he used severe statutes and deep slander, harming many.

sentences.zh: 有言其挾私詆欺不專平者，上以方進所舉應科，不以為非也。

translations.literal: When some said he bore private grudges, slandered and deceived, and was not solely fair, the emperor held that what Fangjin had reported matched the statutes and did not regard it as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When some said he bore private grudges, slandered unjustly, and was not impartial, the emperor held that Fangjin's reports matched the statutes and did not regard them as wrong.

sentences.zh: 光，褒成君霸之少子也，領尚書，典樞機十餘年，守法度，修故事，上有所問，據經法，以心所安而對，不希指苟合；

translations.literal: Guang was the youngest son of Lord Bao of Baocheng; he headed the Masters of Writing and managed the inner pivot for more than ten years, observed laws and standards, and followed precedents. When the emperor questioned him, he answered according to canonical law as his heart found secure, not currying favor to suit whims;
translations.idiomatic: Guang was the youngest son of Lord Bao of Baocheng. He headed the Masters of Writing and managed the inner pivot for more than ten years, observed law and precedent, and when the emperor questioned him answered according to canonical law as his conscience dictated, not currying favor;

sentences.zh: 如或不從，不敢強諫爭，以是久而安。

translations.literal: if the emperor did not follow, he did not dare forcefully remonstrate and contend, and by this remained secure for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: if the emperor did not follow, he did not dare remonstrate forcefully, and by this remained secure for years.

sentences.zh: 時有所言，輒削草蒿，以為章主之過以奸忠直，人臣大罪也。

translations.literal: Whenever he had spoken on something, he would cut away the draft stalks, holding that to display the lord's faults to expose loyal straightness was a great crime for a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had spoken on something he would destroy his draft, holding that to display the ruler's faults in order to expose loyal straightness was a great crime for a minister.

sentences.zh: 有所薦舉，唯恐其人之聞知。

translations.literal: When he had recommendations, he feared above all that the person would learn of it.
translations.idiomatic: When he recommended someone he feared above all that the person would learn of it.

sentences.zh: 沐日歸休，兄弟妻子燕語，終不及朝省政事。

translations.literal: On bath days when he returned to rest, he talked pleasantly with brothers, wife, and children and never touched court and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his rest days he talked pleasantly with brothers, wife, and children and never mentioned court affairs.

sentences.zh: 或問光：「溫室省中樹，皆何木也？

translations.literal: Someone asked Guang: "The trees in the Greenhouse Office—what kinds of wood are they all?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Guang, "The trees in the Greenhouse Office—what kinds are they?

sentences.zh: 」光嘿不應，更答以它語，其不洩如是。

translations.literal: " Guang was silent and did not answer, but replied with other words; his refusal to leak was like this.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang was silent and did not answer, but replied with other words; such was his refusal to disclose palace matters.

sentences.zh: 上行幸雍，祠五畤。

translations.literal: The emperor traveled in person to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traveled to Yong and sacrificed at the Five Altars.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍王商惡陳湯，奏「湯妄言昌陵且復發徙；

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Shang hated Chen Tang and memorialized, "Tang falsely said Changling would again be opened for relocation;
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Wang Shang hated Chen Tang and memorialized that Tang had falsely said Changling would again be opened for relocation;

sentences.zh: 又言黑龍冬出，微行數出之應。

translations.literal: he also said a black dragon appeared in winter—the omen of the emperor's secret outings in great number."
translations.idiomatic: and had also said a black dragon appeared in winter—the omen matching the emperor's many secret outings."

sentences.zh: 」廷尉奏「湯非所宣言，大不敬。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Justice memorialized, "What Tang said was not what he should have declared—great irreverence."
translations.idiomatic: " The Minister of Justice memorialized that what Tang had said was not what he should have declared—great irreverence.

sentences.zh: 」詔以湯有功，免為庶人，徙邊。

translations.literal: " An edict held that because Tang had merit, he was dismissed to commoner status and banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict held that because Tang had merit, he was reduced to commoner status and banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 上以趙後之立也，淳于長有力焉，故德之，乃追顯其前白罷昌陵之功，下公卿，議封長。

translations.literal: Because the emperor's establishment of Empress Zhao had owed much to Chunyu Chang, he favored him and thereupon posthumously displayed his earlier merit in reporting to stop Changling, sent the matter down to the excellencies and ministers, and discussed enfeoffing Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Empress Zhao's elevation had owed much to Chunyu Chang, the emperor favored him and posthumously recognized his earlier merit in urging the abandonment of Changling, referred the matter to the excellencies and ministers, and discussed enfeoffing Chang.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳平當以為：「長雖有善言，不應封爵之科。

translations.literal: Household Grandee Ping Dang held: "Although Chang had good words, they do not meet the category for enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: Household Grandee Ping Dang held that although Chang had spoken well, it did not meet the category for enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 」當坐左遷巨鹿太守。

translations.literal: " Dang was punished by demotion to Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: " Dang was demoted to Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 上遂下詔，以常侍閎，侍中、衛尉長首建至策，賜長、閎爵關內侯。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict: because Regular Attendant Hong and Palace Attendant and Commandant of Guards Chang had first proposed the supreme plan, he granted Chang and Hong the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon issued an edict granting Marquis within the Passes to Chunyu Chang and Regular Attendant Hong for having first proposed the supreme plan.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠萬年佞邪不忠，毒流眾庶，與陳湯俱徒敦煌。

translations.literal: Chief Artisan for Palace Construction Wannian was fawning, wicked, and disloyal; his poison spread among the masses. He and Chen Tang were both banished to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Artisan for Palace Construction Wannian was fawning, wicked, and disloyal, and his harm spread among the people. He and Chen Tang were both banished to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 初，少府陳咸，衛尉逢信，官簿皆在翟方進之右；

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister Steward Chen Xian and Commandant of Guards Feng Xin both ranked above Zhai Fangjin on the official registers;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Minister Steward Chen Xian and Commandant of Guards Feng Xin had both ranked above Zhai Fangjin on the official registers;

sentences.zh: 方進晚進，為京兆尹，與咸厚善。

translations.literal: Fangjin entered late, became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and was on close terms with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fangjin had entered service later; as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao he was on close terms with Xian.

sentences.zh: 及御史大夫缺，三人皆名卿，俱在選中，而方進得之。

translations.literal: When the Censor-in-Chief's office was vacant, all three were renowned ministers and were all in the selection, yet Fangjin obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor-in-chiefship fell vacant, all three were renowned ministers and all were candidates, yet Fangjin obtained the post.

sentences.zh: 會丞相薛宣得罪，與方進相連，上使五二千石雜問丞相、御史，咸詰責方進，冀得其處，方進心恨。

translations.literal: It happened that Chancellor Xue Xuan offended and was implicated with Fangjin; the emperor sent various officials at two-thousand-bushel rank jointly to question the chancellor and censor. Xian pressed and blamed Fangjin, hoping to catch him out; Fangjin bore resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Xue Xuan offended and was implicated with Fangjin, the emperor sent various two-thousand-bushel officials jointly to question chancellor and censor. Xian pressed and blamed Fangjin, hoping to catch him out; Fangjin resented it.

sentences.zh: 陳湯素以材能得幸於王鳳及王音，咸、信皆與湯善，湯數稱之於鳳、音所，以此得為九卿。

translations.literal: Chen Tang had long won favor through talent with Wang Feng and Wang Yin; Xian and Xin were both friendly with Tang, and Tang repeatedly praised them in Feng's and Yin's presence, by which they came to be among the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang had long won favor through talent with Wang Feng and Wang Yin. Xian and Xin were both friendly with Tang, and Tang repeatedly praised them to Feng and Yin, by which they rose to the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 及王商黜逐湯，方進因奏「咸、信附會湯以求薦舉，苟得無恥。

translations.literal: When Wang Shang dismissed and drove out Tang, Fangjin thereupon memorialized, "Xian and Xin attached themselves to Tang to seek recommendation—shameless in grasping gain."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shang dismissed Tang, Fangjin memorialized that Xian and Xin had attached themselves to Tang to seek recommendation—shameless opportunists.

sentences.zh: 」皆免官。

translations.literal: " Both were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Both were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 是歲，琅邪太守朱博為左馮翊。

translations.literal: That year, Administrator of Langye Zhu Bo became Left Governor of the Metropolitan Area.
translations.idiomatic: That year Administrator of Langye Zhu Bo became Left Governor of the Metropolitan Area.

sentences.zh: 博治郡，常令屬縣各用其豪桀以為大吏，文、武從宜。

translations.literal: Bo governed the commandery by often ordering subordinate counties each to employ their powerful and outstanding men as chief officials, civil and military as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Bo governed his commandery by often ordering each subordinate county to employ its powerful local leaders as chief officials, assigning civil or military duties as fit.

sentences.zh: 縣有劇賊及它非常，博輒移書以詭責之，其盡力有效，必加厚賞；

translations.literal: When a county had fierce bandits or other extraordinary matters, Bo would send a letter with subtle blame; if they exerted themselves with effect, he always added heavy rewards;
translations.idiomatic: When a county had fierce bandits or other emergencies, Bo would send a subtly worded letter of rebuke; if they exerted themselves with success he always rewarded them heavily;

sentences.zh: 懷詐不稱，誅罰輒行。

translations.literal: if they harbored deceit and did not measure up, execution and punishment were immediately carried out.
translations.idiomatic: if they were deceitful and failed to measure up, punishment followed at once.

sentences.zh: 以是豪強懾服，事無不集。

translations.literal: By this the powerful were awed into submission and nothing failed to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: By this the powerful were awed into submission and nothing failed to get done.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己卯晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the last day of the cycle jimao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the last day of jimao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 初，帝用匡衡議，罷甘泉泰畤，其日，大風壞甘泉竹宮，折拔畤中樹木十圍以上百餘。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had followed Kuang Heng's proposal and abolished the Grand Unity altar at Ganquan. That day a great wind destroyed Ganquan's bamboo palace and broke and uprooted more than a hundred trees of ten arm-spans or more within the altars.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had followed Kuang Heng's proposal and abolished the Grand Unity altar at Ganquan. That day a great wind destroyed Ganquan's bamboo palace and broke more than a hundred trees of ten arm-spans or more within the altars.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，以問劉向，對曰：「家人尚不欲絕種祠，況於國之神寶舊畤！

translations.literal: The emperor thought it strange and asked Liu Xiang. He replied, saying: "Even a household does not wish to cut off ancestral sacrifices—how much more the state's divine treasures and old altars!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought it strange and asked Liu Xiang, who replied, "Even a household does not wish to cut off ancestral sacrifices—how much more the state's divine treasures and old altars!

sentences.zh: 且甘泉、汾陰及雍五畤始立，皆有神示氐感應，然後營之，非苟而已也。

translations.literal: Moreover Ganquan, Fenyin, and Yong's Five Altars, when first established, all had divine manifestations and responses from the people, and only then were they built—not done casually.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Ganquan, Fenyin, and Yong's Five Altars were first established only after divine manifestations and popular responses, and were not built casually.

sentences.zh: 武、宣之世奉此三神，禮敬敕備，神光尤著。

translations.literal: In the eras of Wu and Xuan these three spirits were served; ritual reverence was ordered complete, and divine radiance was especially manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eras of Emperor Wu and Emperor Xuan these three spirits were served with complete ritual reverence, and divine radiance was especially manifest.

sentences.zh: 祖宗所立神祇舊位，誠未易動。

translations.literal: The old positions of the spirits established by the ancestors are truly not easy to move.
translations.idiomatic: The old positions of the spirits established by the ancestors are truly not easy to move.

sentences.zh: 前始納貢禹之議，後人相因，多所動搖。

translations.literal: Earlier you first accepted Gong Yu's proposal; later men followed one another and moved many things.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier you first accepted Gong Yu's proposal; later men followed suit and moved many things.

sentences.zh: 《易大傳》曰：『誣神者殃及三世。

translations.literal: The Great Commentary on the Changes says: 'Those who slander the spirits bring calamity on three generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Commentary on the Changes says, 'Those who slander the spirits bring calamity on three generations.

sentences.zh: 』恐其咎不獨止禹等！

translations.literal: ' I fear the blame will not stop with Yu and the rest alone!"
translations.idiomatic: ' I fear the blame will not stop with Yu and his followers alone!"

sentences.zh: 」上意恨之，又以久無繼嗣，冬，十月，庚辰，上白太后，令詔有司復甘泉泰畤、汾陰后土如故，及雍五畤、陳寶祠、長安及郡國祠著明者，皆復之。

translations.literal: " The emperor resented this in his mind; also because he had long lacked an heir—in winter, tenth month, on gengchen—he informed the Empress Dowager and ordered an edict to the relevant offices to restore the Grand Unity altar at Ganquan, the Queen of Earth at Fenyin, and the rest as before, and also Yong's Five Altars, the Chen Treasure shrine, and notable shrines in Chang'an and the commanderies and kingdoms—all were restored.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor resented this; also because he had long lacked an heir—in winter, the tenth month, on gengchen—he informed the Empress Dowager and ordered the relevant offices to restore the Grand Unity altar at Ganquan, the Queen of Earth at Fenyin, Yong's Five Altars, the Chen Treasure shrine, and notable shrines in Chang'an and throughout the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 是時，上以無繼嗣，頗好鬼神、方術之屬，上書言祭祀方術得待詔者甚眾，祠祭費用頗多。

translations.literal: At this time, because the emperor had no heir, he rather favored ghosts and spirits and the class of occult arts; those who submitted memorials on sacrifices and occult arts and obtained attendance at audience were very numerous, and the expenses of shrine sacrifice were rather great.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, because the emperor had no heir, he favored ghosts, spirits, and occult arts; many who submitted memorials on sacrifices and occult techniques obtained audience at court, and sacrificial expenses grew heavy.

sentences.zh: 谷永說上曰：「臣聞明於天地之性，不可惑以神怪；

translations.literal: Gu Yong admonished the emperor, saying: "Your servant has heard that one clear about the nature of Heaven and Earth cannot be deluded by spirits and marvels;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong admonished the emperor, saying, "Your servant has heard that one who understands the nature of Heaven and Earth cannot be deluded by spirits and marvels;

sentences.zh: 知萬物之情，不可罔以非類。

translations.literal: one who knows the conditions of the myriad things cannot be misled by improper kinds.
translations.idiomatic: one who knows the conditions of the myriad things cannot be misled by improper kinds.

sentences.zh: 諸背仁義之正道，不遵《五經》之法言，而盛稱奇怪鬼神，廣崇祭祀之方，求報無福之祠，及言世有仙人，服食不終之藥，遙興輕舉、黃治變化之術者，皆奸人惑眾，挾左道，懷詐偽，以欺罔世主。

translations.literal: All who turn their backs on the correct path of benevolence and righteousness, do not follow the law-words of the Five Classics, yet loudly praise strange ghosts and spirits, broadly exalt methods of sacrifice, seek reward from shrines without blessing, and speak of immortals in the world, drugs taken without end, arts of soaring lightly from afar, and yellow-elixir transformation—all are wicked men deluding the masses, clutching heterodox ways, harboring fraud and falsehood to deceive and mislead the age's lord.
translations.idiomatic: All who abandon the righteous path, ignore the teachings of the Five Classics, yet loudly praise strange ghosts and spirits, broadly promote sacrificial arts, seek blessings from shrines that confer none, or speak of worldly immortals, deathless drugs, levitation, and yellow-elixir transformation—all are wicked men deluding the people, clutching heterodox ways and fraud to deceive their ruler.

sentences.zh: 聽其言，洋洋滿耳，若將可遇，求之，蕩蕩如繫風捕景，終不可得。

translations.literal: Hear their words and they fill the ear grandly, as if one might soon encounter them; seek them and it is vast and empty like tying the wind and catching shadows—in the end nothing can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Hear their words and they fill the ear grandly, as if immortals were near at hand; seek them and it is like tying the wind or catching shadows—nothing can be obtained in the end.

sentences.zh: 是以明王距而不聽，聖人絕而不語。

translations.literal: Therefore enlightened kings reject them and do not listen; sages cut them off and do not speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore enlightened kings reject them and do not listen; sages cut them off and do not speak of them.

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇使徐福發男女入海求神采藥，因逃不還，天下怨恨。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin Shihuang sent Xu Fu with men and women launched into the sea to seek spirit-color drugs; they fled and did not return, and All-under-Heaven resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Qin Shihuang sent Xu Fu with men and women to sea to seek elixir; they fled and never returned, and the realm resented it.

sentences.zh: 漢興，新垣平、齊人少翁、公孫卿、欒大等皆以術窮詐得，誅夷伏辜。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Xinyuan Ping, the Qi man Shaoweng, Gongsun Qing, Luan Da, and others all exhausted their arts in fraud and were obtained, executed, exterminated, and paid guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, Xinyuan Ping, Shaoweng of Qi, Gongsun Qing, Luan Da, and others all exhausted their arts in fraud, were exposed, and were executed.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下距絕此類，毋令奸人有以窺朝者！

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty reject and cut off this class, and not let wicked men have means to peer into the court!
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty alone reject this whole class, and not let wicked men find a way to peer into the court!

sentences.zh: 」上善其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 十一月，尉氏男子樊並等十三人謀反，殺陳留太守，劫略吏民，自稱將軍；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, the men of Weishi—Fan Bing and thirteen others—plotted rebellion, killed the Administrator of Chenliu, robbed officials and people, and styled themselves generals;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Fan Bing of Weishi and thirteen others plotted rebellion, killed the Administrator of Chenliu, robbed officials and commoners, and styled themselves generals;

sentences.zh: 徒李潭、稱忠、鍾祖、訾順共殺並，以聞，皆封為侯。

translations.literal: convict laborers Li Tan, Cheng Zhong, Zhong Zu, and Zi Shun together killed Bing and reported it; all were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: convict laborers Li Tan, Cheng Zhong, Zhong Zu, and Zi Shun together killed Bing and reported it; all were enfeoffed as marquises.

sentences.zh: 十二月，山陽鐵官徙蘇令等二百二十八人攻殺長吏，盜庫兵，自稱將軍；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the iron-office convicts of Shanyang—Su Ling and two hundred twenty-eight others—attacked and killed chief officials, stole arsenal weapons, and styled themselves generals;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, iron-office convicts of Shanyang—Su Ling and two hundred twenty-eight others—attacked and killed chief officials, stole arsenal weapons, and styled themselves generals;

sentences.zh: 經郡國十九，殺東郡太守及汝南都尉。

translations.literal: they passed through nineteen commanderies and kingdoms and killed the Administrator of Dongjun and the Commandant of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: they passed through nineteen commanderies and kingdoms and killed the Administrator of Dongjun and the Commandant of Runan.

sentences.zh: 汝南太守嚴訢捕斬令等。

translations.literal: Administrator of Runan Yan Xin captured and beheaded Ling and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Runan Yan Xin captured and beheaded Su Ling and his followers.

sentences.zh: 遷訢為大司農。

translations.literal: Xin was transferred to be Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xin was transferred to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 故南昌尉九江梅福上書曰：「昔高祖納善若不及，從諫如轉圜，聽言不求其能，舉功不考其素，陳平起於亡命而為謀主，韓信拔於行陳而建上將；

translations.literal: The former Nanchang commandant Mei Fu of Jiujiang submitted a memorial, saying: "In former times Gaozu received the good as if he could not catch up, followed remonstrance as if turning a disk; he listened to words without demanding ability, raised achievement without examining past conduct. Chen Ping rose from outlaw status and became chief strategist; Han Xin was pulled from the ranks and established as chief general;"
translations.idiomatic: The former Nanchang commandant Mei Fu of Jiujiang submitted a memorial, saying, "Formerly Gaozu received good counsel as if he could never catch up and followed remonstrance as if turning a wheel; he listened without demanding talent and promoted achievement without examining past conduct. Chen Ping rose from outlaw status to become chief strategist; Han Xin was pulled from the ranks to become chief general;"

sentences.zh: 故天下之士雲合歸漢，爭進奇異，知者竭其策，愚者盡其慮，勇士極其節，怯夫勉其死。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentlemen of the realm gathered like clouds to return to Han, vying to advance the strange and new; the wise exhausted their stratagems, the foolish gave all their thought, braves exerted their integrity, and cowards strove to their death.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the realm's worthies gathered like clouds to serve Han, each vying to offer something extraordinary; the wise exhausted their stratagems, the foolish gave all their counsel, the brave gave their utmost loyalty, and even cowards strove unto death.

sentences.zh: 合天下之知，並天下之威，是以舉秦如鴻毛，取楚若拾遺，此高祖所以無敵於天下也。

translations.literal: Joining all-under-Heaven's knowledge and combining all-under-Heaven's might, thus he raised Qin like a goose feather and took Chu as if picking up what was lost—this is why Gaozu was without peer in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Combining the wisdom and might of the realm, he overthrew Qin as lightly as lifting a goose feather and took Chu as if picking up what was lost—this is why Gaozu was without peer under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝好忠諫，說至言，出爵不待廉、茂，慶賜不須顯功，是以天下布衣各厲志竭精以赴闕廷，自衒鬻者不可勝數，漢家得賢，於此為盛。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu loved loyal remonstrance and delighted in utmost words; he issued ranks without waiting for incorruptibility and florid virtue, bestowed rewards without requiring manifest achievement—thus the common-cloth of all the realm each sharpened will and exhausted spirit to attend court; those who advertised and sold themselves were beyond counting; Han obtained worthies, and here it was most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu loved loyal remonstrance and delighted in forthright speech; he granted ranks without waiting for provincial nominations, bestowed rewards without requiring conspicuous merit, and so commoners across the realm each sharpened their will and exhausted their spirit to come to court. Those who touted themselves were beyond counting; Han obtained talent at its peak.

sentences.zh: 使孝武皇帝聽用其計，昇平可致，於是積屍暴骨，快心胡、越，故淮南王安緣間而起；

translations.literal: If Emperor Xiaowu had listened and employed their plans, ascending peace could have been attained; but instead corpses piled and bones were exposed, he gratified his heart with Hu and Yue, and therefore Huainan king Liu An seized the opening and rose;
translations.idiomatic: Had Emperor Wu fully heeded their counsel, lasting peace could have been achieved; instead corpses piled and bones lay exposed as he gratified himself with campaigns against the Hu and Yue, and therefore King An of Huainan seized the opening and rose in rebellion;

sentences.zh: 所以計慮不成而謀議洩者，以眾賢聚於本朝，故其大臣勢陵，不敢和從也。

translations.literal: the reason his schemes did not succeed and his counsels leaked was that many worthies were gathered at the central court, so his great ministers' power was overawed and dared not harmonize and follow.
translations.idiomatic: the reason his plots failed and his counsels leaked was that so many worthies were gathered at the central court that his great ministers were overawed and dared not join him.

sentences.zh: 方今布衣乃窺國家之隙，見間而起者，蜀郡是也。

translations.literal: Now commoners spy the state's gaps; those who rise at an opening—Shu Commandery is an example.
translations.idiomatic: Today commoners spy the state's weaknesses; those who rise when they see an opening include Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 及山陽亡徒蘇令之群，蹈藉名都、大郡，求黨與，索隨和，而亡逃匿之意，此皆輕量大臣，無所畏忌，國家之權輕，故匹夫欲與上爭衡也。

translations.literal: And the band of convict laborers of Shanyang such as Su Ling—trampling famous capitals and great commanderies, seeking partisans, demanding Sui and He jade—and without intent to flee and hide: all these lightly weigh the great ministers, have nothing to fear, the state's authority is light, and therefore common men wish to contend balance with the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: And the band of Shanyang convicts led by Su Ling—trampling famous capitals and great commanderies, seeking allies, demanding precious jade, with no thought of fleeing and hiding—all show that they lightly regard great ministers, fear nothing, and find the state's authority slight; therefore common men wish to contend with the throne.

sentences.zh: 士者，國之重器。

translations.literal: Gentlemen are the state's heavy vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent are the state's weightiest vessels.

sentences.zh: 得士則重，失士則輕。

translations.literal: Gain gentlemen and it is heavy; lose gentlemen and it is light.
translations.idiomatic: Gain them and the state is weighty; lose them and it is light.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『濟濟多士，文王以寧。

translations.literal: The Odes says: 'Abundant are the many officers; King Wen thereby had peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says, 'Abundant are the many officers; King Wen thereby had peace.

sentences.zh: 』廟堂之議，非草茅所言也。

translations.literal: ' Deliberations in the ancestral temple hall are not what thatch and grass may speak of.
translations.idiomatic: ' Deliberations in the ancestral temple are not for thatched-hut commoners to speak of.

sentences.zh: 臣誠恐身塗野草，屍並卒伍，故數上書求見，輒報罷。

translations.literal: Your servant truly fears that my body will be smeared on wild plants and my corpse lie among the ranks, therefore I have repeatedly submitted memorials seeking audience, but each time am answered with dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly fears my body will be left on the wild grass and my corpse lie among common soldiers; therefore I have repeatedly submitted memorials seeking audience, but each time am dismissed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞齊桓之時，有以九九見者，桓公不逆，欲以致大也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the time of Duke Huan of Qi, there was one who came forward with the nine-nines of arithmetic; Duke Huan did not turn him away, wishing to attain the great thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that in Duke Huan of Qi's time, a man came forward to teach the multiplication table; Duke Huan did not turn him away, wishing thereby to attain great things.

sentences.zh: 今臣所言，非特九九也，陛下距臣者三矣，此天下士所以不至也。

translations.literal: Now what your servant speaks is not merely the nine-nines; Your Majesty has kept your distance from your servant three times—this is why gentlemen of the realm do not come.
translations.idiomatic: What your servant speaks is far more than the multiplication table, yet Your Majesty has kept your distance three times—this is why men of talent do not come.

sentences.zh: 昔秦武王好力，任鄙叩關自鬻；

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu of Qin loved strength; Ren Bi knocked at the passes to sell himself;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly King Wu of Qin loved strength; Ren Bi knocked at the passes to offer his services;

sentences.zh: 繆公行伯，由余歸德。

translations.literal: Duke Mu executed hegemony; You Yu returned his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu achieved hegemony when You Yu came and submitted his virtue.

sentences.zh: 今欲致天下之士，民有上書求見者，輒使詣尚書問其所言，言可採取者，秩以升斗之祿，賜以一束之帛，若此，則天下之士，發憤懣，吐忠言，嘉謀日聞於上，天下條貫，國家表裡，爛然可睹矣。

translations.literal: Now if you wish to bring worthies of the realm, when the people have memorials seeking audience, immediately have them go to the Masters of Writing to question what they said; for words that may be adopted, rank them with a sheng or dou of salary, grant a bundle of silk—if like this, then gentlemen of the realm will release indignation, speak loyal words, good plans daily heard above, the realm's threads strung through, state's inside and outside, brilliantly visible.
translations.idiomatic: If you now wish to bring worthies of the realm, whenever someone submits a memorial seeking audience, have him go at once to the Masters of Writing to state his case; for words that may be adopted, grant a modest salary and a bundle of silk. If you do this, men of talent will release their indignation, speak loyal words, and good counsel will daily reach the throne; the realm's affairs and the state's inner and outer condition will shine clear.

sentences.zh: 夫以四海之廣，士民之數，能言之類至眾多也；

translations.literal: With the four seas' breadth and the number of gentlemen and people, the class that can speak is extremely many;
translations.idiomatic: With the breadth of the four seas and the number of gentlemen and commoners, those who can speak are exceedingly many;

sentences.zh: 然其俊桀指世陳政，言成文章，質之先聖而不繆，施之當世合時務，若此者亦無幾人。

translations.literal: yet among them the outstanding who point at the age and lay out government, whose words form compositions, when tested against former sages are not wrong, when applied to the present age accord with the times' tasks—of such there are also hardly any.
translations.idiomatic: yet those outstanding enough to address the age, set forth policy in finished prose, stand testing against the former sages without error, and fit the present age's needs—such men are very few.

sentences.zh: 故爵祿束帛者，天下之砥石，高祖所以厲世摩鈍也。

translations.literal: Therefore ranks, salaries, and bundles of silk are the realm's whetstone—what Gaozu used to sharpen the age and grind the blunt.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ranks, salaries, and bundles of silk are the realm's whetstone—what Gaozu used to sharpen the age and grind the dull.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『工欲善其事，必先利其器。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'If a craftsman wishes to do his work well, he must first sharpen his tools.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'If a craftsman wishes to do his work well, he must first sharpen his tools.

sentences.zh: 』至秦則不然，張誹謗之罔以為漢驅除，倒持泰阿，授楚其柄。

translations.literal: ' But Qin was not so: it spread the net of slander to drive out for Han, held Tai'e inverted, and handed Chu the handle.
translations.idiomatic: ' But Qin did otherwise: it spread the net of slander, which ended by clearing the way for Han; it held the great sword Tai'e by the blade and handed Chu the handle.

sentences.zh: 故誠能勿失其柄，天下雖有不順，莫敢觸其鋒，此孝武皇帝所以闢地建功，為漢世宗也。

translations.literal: Therefore if one can truly not lose the handle, though all-under-Heaven has those not compliant, none dares touch his edge—this is why Emperor Xiaowu opened territory and established achievement, and became Han's lineage ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if one truly does not lose the handle, though the realm has the unruly, none dares touch his edge—this is why Emperor Wu opened territory, established achievement, and became Han's lineage temple name.

sentences.zh: 「今陛下既不納天下之言，又加戮焉。

translations.literal: "Now Your Majesty neither accepts the words of the realm, and moreover adds slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: "Now Your Majesty will not accept the realm's words, and on top of that adds executions.

sentences.zh: 夫鳶鵲遭害，則仁鳥增逝，愚者蒙戮，則智士深退。

translations.literal: When kites and magpies meet harm, then benevolent birds increasingly flee; when fools receive execution, then wise men deeply withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When kites and magpies meet harm, benevolent birds flee all the more; when fools are executed, wise men withdraw deeply.

sentences.zh: 間者愚民上疏，多觸不急之法，或下廷尉而死者眾。

translations.literal: Recently foolish commoners submitted memorials, many touching urgent-not laws; some sent down to the Minister of Justice—and the dead were many.
translations.idiomatic: Recently foolish commoners submitted memorials, many violating petty statutes; many were sent down to the Minister of Justice and died.

sentences.zh: 自陽朔以來，天下以言為諱，朝廷尤甚，群臣皆承順上指，莫有執正。

translations.literal: Since the Yangshuo era, the realm has taken speech as taboo—the court especially so; the ministers all follow and accord with the sovereign's intent, none holding correct.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yangshuo era the realm has tabooed speech, the court especially so; the ministers all follow the sovereign's intent, none holding firm to what is right.

sentences.zh: 何以明其然也？

translations.literal: How to make clear that it is so?
translations.idiomatic: How may one prove that this is so?

sentences.zh: 取民所上書，陛下之所善，試下之廷尉，廷尉必曰『非所宜言，大不敬，』以此卜之，一矣。

translations.literal: Take the people's submitted memorials that Your Majesty favors, try sending them down to the Minister of Justice—the Minister of Justice will certainly say 'not what should be spoken—great irreverence'; test by this and it will be one.
translations.idiomatic: Take any memorial the people submit that Your Majesty favors and try sending it down to the Minister of Justice—the Minister of Justice will certainly say, 'Not what should be spoken—great irreverence.' Test it thus and you will find it always so.

sentences.zh: 故京兆尹王章，資質忠直，敢面引廷爭，孝元皇帝擢之，以厲具臣而矯曲朝；

translations.literal: Therefore Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao Wang Zhang, by nature loyal and straight, dared face-to-face citation and court contention; Emperor Xiaoyuan promoted him, to encourage ordinary ministers and straighten the crooked court;
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Governor Wang Zhang was by nature loyal and upright and dared remonstrate face to face at court; Emperor Yuan promoted him to encourage ordinary ministers and straighten a crooked court;

sentences.zh: 及至陛下，戮及妻子。

translations.literal: but when it reached Your Majesty, execution extended to wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: but under Your Majesty execution extended to his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 且惡惡止其身，王章非有反畔之辜而殃及室家，折直士之節，結諫臣之舌。

translations.literal: Moreover, hate evil and stop at the person himself—Wang Zhang had no guilt of rebellion and rebellion yet calamity reached household and family; this breaks the integrity of straight gentlemen and knots the tongues of remonstrating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when one hates evil one should stop at the person himself; Wang Zhang had no crime of rebellion, yet calamity reached his household. This breaks the integrity of upright men and ties the tongues of remonstrating ministers.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆知其非，然不敢爭，天下以言為戒，最國家之大患也！

translations.literal: The ministers all know it was wrong, yet none dared contend—the realm takes speech as warning; it is the state's greatest calamity!
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all know it was wrong, yet none dared contend; the realm takes speech as a warning—this is the state's greatest calamity!

sentences.zh: 願陛下循高祖之軌，杜亡秦之路，除不急之法，下無諱之詔，博覽兼聽，謀及疏賤，令深者不隱，遠者不塞，所謂『闢四門，明四目』也。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty follow Gaozu's track, block Qin's path of perdition, remove not-urgent laws, issue an edict without taboo, broadly view and jointly listen, take counsel even from the remote and base, make the deep not hide and the far not blocked—what is called 'open the four gates, clarify the four eyes.'
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty follow Gaozu's course, block Qin's road to ruin, abolish petty statutes, issue an edict free of taboo, broadly view and jointly listen, take counsel even from the remote and humble, so the deep do not hide and the distant are not blocked—what is called 'open the four gates and clarify the four eyes.'

sentences.zh: 往者不可及，來者猶可追。

translations.literal: What is past cannot be reached; what comes may still be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The past cannot be reached, but what is to come may still be pursued.

sentences.zh: 方今君命犯而主威奪，外戚之權，日以益隆。

translations.literal: Just now the lord's mandate is violated and the master's awe is seized; the power of maternal kin daily grows more lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Just now the ruler's command is violated and the sovereign's authority seized; the power of the maternal kin grows more exalted day by day.

sentences.zh: 陛下不見其形，願察其景！

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not see its form—may you inspect its shadow!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not see its form—may you inspect its shadow!

sentences.zh: 建始以來，日食、地震，以率言之，三倍春秋，水災亡與比數，陰盛陽微，金鐵為飛，此何景也？

translations.literal: Since Jianshi began, solar eclipses and earthquakes—reckoned by rate, three times the Spring and Autumn; floods without compare in number; yin flourishing, yang slight; metal and iron flying—what shadow is this?
translations.idiomatic: Since Jianshi began, solar eclipses and earthquakes have occurred, by rate, three times as often as in the Spring and Autumn Annals; floods without parallel; yin flourishing and yang declining; metal and iron flying through the air—what shadow is this?

sentences.zh: 漢興以來，社稷三危：呂，霍，上官；

translations.literal: Since Han arose, the altars of state have thrice been in peril: the Lü, the Huo, the Shangguan;
translations.idiomatic: Since Han arose the altars of state have thrice been imperiled: by the Lü, the Huo, and the Shangguan clans;

sentences.zh: 皆母后之家也。

translations.literal: all were families of empress dowagers.
translations.idiomatic: all were families of empresses dowager.

sentences.zh: 親親之道，全之為右，當與之賢師良傅，教以忠孝之道。

translations.literal: The Way of treating kin as kin—preserving them completely is supreme; one should give them worthy teachers and good tutors, instruct them in the Way of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: In the Way of treating kin as kin, preserving them whole is supreme; they should be given worthy teachers and good tutors and instructed in loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 今乃尊寵其位，授以魁柄，使之驕逆，至於夷滅，此失親親之大者也。

translations.literal: Now you honor and favor their position, confer on them the chief handle, make them arrogant and defiant, until extermination—this is the great failure of treating kin as kin.
translations.idiomatic: Now you honor and favor their position, confer the chief handle on them, make them arrogant and defiant, until extermination—this is the great failure of the Way of kin.

sentences.zh: 自霍光之賢，不能為子孫慮，故權臣易世則危。

translations.literal: Even from Huo Guang's worth, he could not plan for descendants—therefore when power-ministers change generations, it is peril.
translations.idiomatic: Even Huo Guang at his worthiest could not plan for his descendants; therefore when power-holding ministers pass to a new generation, peril follows.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『毋若火，始庸庸。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'Do not be like fire, at first smoldering smoldering.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, 'Do not be like fire, at first only smoldering.

sentences.zh: 』勢陵於君，權隆於主，然後防之，亦無及已！

translations.literal: ' When power overtops the lord and authority towers above the master, only then to guard against it—already too late!
translations.idiomatic: ' When power overtops the lord and authority towers above the sovereign, only then to guard against it—already too late!

sentences.zh: 」上不納。

translations.literal: " The sovereign did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not accept it.
